guides.title: 傳力、算例與驗證：巨厚筏基水化熱控制
guides.titleEn: Load paths, calculations and verification: Hydration-heat control in massive raft foundations
guides.concept: 超高層的筏基厚達數公尺、一次連續澆置數萬立方公尺，水泥水化放出的熱量幾乎全部困在核心，表面卻持續散熱，造成高溫與內外溫差。本課以上海中心大廈約 6 萬 m³ 的連續澆置、天津高銀金融 117 的 65,000 m³ 筏基與洛杉磯 Wilshire Grand Center 的約 5.5 m 厚筏基為例，說明溫升估算、約束應力、低熱配比、冷卻管、連續供料與分層、保溫養護、熱電偶監測、模型校正、延遲鈣礬石風險與溫控紀錄交接。
guides.conceptEn: Supertall rafts are several metres thick and placed continuously in tens of thousands of cubic metres; hydration heat is trapped almost entirely in the core while the surfaces keep losing heat, creating high temperatures and core-to-surface differentials. Using Shanghai Tower's continuous pour of about 60,000 m³, the 65,000 m³ raft of Goldin Finance 117 in Tianjin and the raft about 5.5 m thick at Wilshire Grand Center in Los Angeles, the course covers temperature-rise estimates, restraint stresses, low-heat mixes, cooling pipes, continuous supply and layering, insulated curing, thermocouple monitoring, model calibration, delayed ettringite risk and handover of thermal-control records.
procedure: 水泥水化是放熱反應，薄板中的熱很快從表面散失，溫度只略為上升；但筏基厚度一旦達到數公尺，核心的熱要穿過數公尺混凝土才能到達表面，散熱時間遠長於放熱時間，核心幾乎處於絕熱狀態。結果是核心溫度接近「澆置溫度加絕熱溫升」，而表面溫度隨氣溫下降，兩者的差距在數天內迅速擴大。ACI 301 第 8 節把這類需要溫度控制的構件列為巨積混凝土，並在契約未另訂時採用最高溫度約 70°C、內外溫差約 19°C 的預設限值。
溫度本身不會造成裂縫，被約束的溫度變形才會。巨積筏基有兩種約束：內部約束來自核心熱膨脹、表面冷收縮，表面被核心拉住而受拉，常在早期造成表面裂縫；外部約束來自筏基底部與既有地盤、樁或先澆混凝土的黏結，整體冷卻收縮時被底部拉住，可能在後期形成貫穿裂縫。早齡混凝土的彈性模數與抗拉強度都在快速成長，所以溫差是否造成裂縫，要比較的是當下的拉應力與當下的抗拉強度。
降低溫升最直接的方法是減少放熱：降低單位水泥量、以飛灰或爐石取代部分水泥、使用中低熱水泥，並以較大粒徑與良好級配的骨材減少漿體量。筏基常以 56 或 90 天齡期定義設計強度，讓含大量摻料的配比有時間發展強度。天津高銀金融 117 的筏基使用 C50P8 混凝土，表示筏基同時需要足夠的強度與抗滲等級；配比必須在低熱、強度、抗滲與可泵性之間取得平衡，而不是只追求最低放熱。
除了減少放熱，也可以主動帶走熱量或降低起始溫度。預埋冷卻水管在澆置後通水，把核心的熱帶出；以冰水、碎冰或液態氮預冷混凝土則降低澆置溫度；分層澆置讓每層有時間散熱。冷卻水管必須控制水溫與流量：水溫太低會在管周形成局部溫差裂縫，停止通水過早則核心再度升溫。冷卻管在完成後要灌漿封堵，避免成為滲水通道。並非所有筏基都使用冷卻管，許多案例只靠低熱配比、預冷與保溫就能達成限值，選擇取決於厚度、配比與工期。

巨厚筏基通常要求一次連續澆置，避免在受力最大的基礎內產生施工縫。這需要龐大的供料與泵送能力：三一重工公布上海中心大廈筏基以約 60 小時澆置約 61,000 m³，天津高銀金融 117 以 18 台拖泵與 4 台車載泵在 80 小時內澆置 65,000 m³；Wilshire Grand Center 在 2014 年 2 月以約 20 小時完成約 16,200 m³ 的連續澆置。連續澆置以斜面分層推進，每一層必須在下層初凝前覆蓋並振搗結合，否則形成冷縫；澆置速度也影響溫度，因為每層暴露散熱的時間不同。
控制內外溫差的關鍵通常不是冷卻核心，而是讓表面保持溫暖：在筏基頂面覆蓋塑膠布防止水分散失，再加上保溫毯或保溫板，減緩表面降溫，使表面溫度跟著核心一起緩慢下降。側面若採用鋼模，保溫效果差，可在模板外加保溫或延後拆模。保溫的拆除時機同樣關鍵：核心仍熱時拆除保溫，表面會在短時間內降到氣溫，溫差瞬間超限；應等到核心、表面與氣溫三者的差距都夠小時，分段逐步拆除。
溫度監測是溫控計畫的回饋迴路。佈點要能抓到最高溫度與最大溫差：筏基平面中央與最厚處的核心、頂面與底面下約 50 mm、側面與角落，以及環境氣溫；冷卻管附近也應設點。每一個核心點都要有對應的表面點，才能直接計算溫差。資料應自動記錄並即時傳輸，設定警戒值與行動值，讓溫控人員在溫差接近限值前就能增加保溫或調整冷卻，而不是事後才發現超限。
熱分析模型的預測依賴許多假設：配比放熱曲線、澆置溫度、表面散熱係數、保溫效果與地盤溫度。實際澆置後的前兩三天，就應以監測資料校正模型：若核心溫升比預測快或高，代表放熱參數或澆置溫度被低估，後續的最高溫度、溫差與保溫拆除時機都要重新預測。分區或分次澆置的筏基，前一次的實測校正可以直接改善下一次的配比與保溫設計。

筏基核心溫度過高，不只造成溫差裂縫，也可能損害混凝土本身。早期溫度若超過約 70°C，水泥水化產物中的鈣礬石可能分解，日後在潮濕環境下延遲再生成（延遲鈣礬石生成，DEF），體積膨脹造成內部裂縫，往往在數年後才出現。這是許多規範把最高溫度定在約 70°C 的主要理由之一；使用適量飛灰或爐石可降低 DEF 風險。筏基長期處於地下水中，正是 DEF 需要的潮濕條件，因此筏基的最高溫度控制比地上構件更重要。
巨厚筏基完成後會被上部結構完全覆蓋，日後幾乎無法檢查；因此在被覆蓋前完成裂縫調查、修補與紀錄是交接的最後機會。調查應繪製裂縫分布圖，記錄寬度、長度與是否貫穿，判定是否需要注入環氧樹脂或其他修補。交接資料包括溫控計畫、配比與放熱試驗、澆置紀錄（時間、方量、各層覆蓋時間）、溫度監測原始資料、模型校正紀錄、不符合事項處理與裂縫修補紀錄，讓業主與未來的結構工程師理解筏基的實際狀態。
procedureEn: Cement hydration releases heat; a thin slab loses it quickly through its surfaces and warms only slightly, but once a raft is several metres thick the core's heat must travel through metres of concrete to escape, so heat loss takes far longer than heat generation and the core is almost adiabatic. The core therefore approaches placing temperature plus adiabatic rise, while the surfaces cool toward air temperature, and the gap widens rapidly over a few days. ACI 301 Section 8 classes such members as mass concrete and, unless the contract states otherwise, uses default limits of about 70°C maximum temperature and about 19°C core-to-surface difference.

Temperature alone does not crack concrete; restrained thermal strain does. A massive raft has two kinds of restraint: internal restraint, where the hot expanding core holds back the cooler contracting surface and puts it in tension, often cracking the surface early; and external restraint from bond to the ground, piles or earlier concrete at the base, which resists overall cooling contraction and can produce through cracks later. Elastic modulus and tensile strength of young concrete are both growing fast, so whether a differential cracks the raft depends on comparing the tensile stress at that moment with the tensile strength at that moment.

The most direct way to cut temperature rise is to release less heat: lower cement content, replace part of the cement with fly ash or slag, use low- or moderate-heat cement, and reduce paste volume with larger, well-graded aggregate. Rafts often define design strength at 56 or 90 days so that mixes with high replacement levels have time to gain strength. The raft of Goldin Finance 117 used C50P8 concrete, showing that rafts also need adequate strength and impermeability; the mix must balance low heat, strength, impermeability and pumpability rather than chase the lowest heat alone.

Besides releasing less heat, heat can be removed actively or the starting temperature lowered. Embedded cooling pipes carry water after placement to draw heat from the core; chilled water, crushed ice or liquid nitrogen pre-cools the concrete and lowers placing temperature; layered placement gives each lift time to lose heat. Cooling pipes need controlled water temperature and flow: water that is too cold creates local differentials and cracks around the pipe, and stopping too early lets the core reheat. Pipes are grouted afterwards so they do not become seepage paths. Not every raft uses cooling pipes; many meet the limits with low-heat mixes, pre-cooling and insulation alone, depending on thickness, mix and programme.

Massive rafts are usually placed in one continuous pour to avoid construction joints in the most heavily loaded part of the foundation. That demands enormous supply and pumping capacity: Sany reports that Shanghai Tower's raft placed about 61,000 m³ in about 60 hours and that Goldin Finance 117 placed 65,000 m³ in 80 hours with 18 trailer pumps and 4 truck pumps, while Wilshire Grand Center completed a continuous pour of about 16,200 m³ in about 20 hours in February 2014. Continuous pours advance in sloping layers, each covered and vibrated into the one below before it sets, or a cold joint forms; placement rate also affects temperature, because each layer is exposed to heat loss for a different time.

The key to controlling differential is usually keeping the surface warm rather than cooling the core: cover the top with plastic sheeting to stop moisture loss, then add insulation blankets or boards to slow surface cooling so that the surface follows the core down slowly. Steel side forms insulate poorly, so add insulation outside them or delay stripping. Removal timing is equally critical: removing insulation while the core is still hot drops the surface to air temperature within hours and the differential instantly exceeds its limit; wait until core, surface and air are all close enough, then remove in stages.

Temperature monitoring is the feedback loop of the thermal-control plan. Sensors must capture peak temperature and maximum differential: the core at the centre and thickest part of the raft, about 50 mm below the top and bottom surfaces, at sides and corners, and ambient air, plus points near cooling pipes. Every core sensor needs a matching surface sensor so the differential can be computed directly. Data should be logged automatically and transmitted live with alert and action thresholds, so that thermal-control staff add insulation or adjust cooling before the differential reaches its limit rather than discovering an exceedance afterwards.

Thermal model predictions rest on many assumptions: the mix heat curve, placing temperature, surface heat-transfer coefficient, insulation performance and ground temperature. Within the first two or three days after placement the model should be calibrated against monitoring data: if the core heats faster or higher than predicted, the heat parameters or placing temperature were underestimated, and peak temperature, differential and insulation-removal timing must all be re-predicted. For rafts placed in zones or stages, calibration from one pour directly improves the mix and insulation design of the next.

An excessively hot raft core risks more than differential cracking; it can damage the concrete itself. If early temperature exceeds about 70°C, ettringite in the hydration products may decompose and later re-form in moist conditions (delayed ettringite formation, DEF), expanding and cracking the concrete internally, often only after several years. This is one of the main reasons many specifications cap maximum temperature at about 70°C, and suitable fly ash or slag contents reduce DEF risk. A raft sits in groundwater for its whole life, exactly the moist condition DEF needs, so peak-temperature control matters even more for rafts than for members above ground.

Once complete, a massive raft is entirely covered by the superstructure and can hardly be inspected again, so finishing the crack survey, repairs and records before it is covered is the last chance at handover. The survey should map cracks, recording width, length and whether they pass through, and decide whether epoxy injection or another repair is needed. Handover records include the thermal-control plan, mix and heat tests, placement logs with times, volumes and layer cover times, raw temperature data, model calibration records, nonconformance actions and crack repair records, so that the owner and future structural engineers understand the raft's real condition.
evidence: 凡厚度超過約 1 m 或膠結料用量高的筏基，都應在契約中指定巨積混凝土條款，要求承包商在澆置前提交溫控計畫，內容包括預測溫度、限值、配比、保溫、監測與超限應變措施，並經結構工程師核准。
溫控計畫要同時規定最高溫度、溫差與降溫速率，並說明外部約束的處理方式（例如滑動層、分區澆置或配置溫度鋼筋）；裂縫寬度允收值與修補方式應事先約定，避免事後爭議。
在結構圖說中允許筏基以 56 或 90 天強度驗收，並明訂摻料種類與比例範圍；材料來源鎖定單一水泥廠與摻料供應商，變更須重新做溫升試驗。
冷卻管配置、進出水溫差上限、通水起訖條件與灌漿封堵方法須寫入溫控計畫，並在澆置前完成水壓試驗作為停檢點；若選擇不用冷卻管，計畫中要說明以預冷與保溫達成限值的依據。
大體積連續澆置屬重大施工節點，需事先由業主、設計、監造與承包商共同審查供料、泵送、交通、照明、人員輪班與緊急應變計畫，並在澆置前一日召開停檢會議確認所有資源就位。
evidenceEn: For any raft thicker than about 1 m or with high binder content, invoke mass-concrete provisions in the contract and require a thermal-control plan before placement, covering predicted temperatures, limits, mix, insulation, monitoring and actions on exceedance, approved by the structural engineer.

The thermal-control plan should set maximum temperature, differential and cooling rate together, explain how external restraint is handled (for example a slip layer, zoned pours or temperature reinforcement), and agree crack-width acceptance and repair methods in advance to avoid disputes later.

Allow raft acceptance at 56 or 90 days in the structural documents with the type and range of supplementary materials stated; lock cement and supplementary material sources to single suppliers, and require new temperature-rise tests for any change.

Write the cooling-pipe layout, the limit on water temperature rise, start and stop criteria and grouting method into the thermal-control plan and make the pressure test a pre-pour hold point; if cooling pipes are not used, the plan must explain how pre-cooling and insulation meet the limits.

A large continuous pour is a major construction milestone; owner, designer, resident engineer and contractor should jointly review supply, pumping, traffic, lighting, shift rotas and contingency plans beforehand, with a hold-point meeting the day before to confirm every resource is in place.
pitfalls: 把筏基當成一般基礎施工，未做溫控計畫，核心溫度超過 80°C、表面在夜間急冷，數天內表面出現網狀或貫穿裂縫，地下水由裂縫滲入，筏基防水與鋼筋耐久都受影響。
為了確保早期強度而提高水泥用量，核心溫度超過限值；或摻料比例過高但未延長設計齡期，28 天強度不合格引發爭議；不同批次飛灰品質變動，放熱與強度發展不一致。
某一預拌廠設備故障或交通管制使供料驟降，斜面上已澆混凝土初凝，新混凝土無法與其結合，形成大面積冷縫；為趕進度集中在少數泵位澆置，某區層厚過大，振搗不足而產生蜂窩。
感測器只裝在核心而未裝表面點，無法判斷溫差；或表面點裝得太深，讀到的溫度偏高，低估實際溫差；資料只在每天上班時下載，夜間溫差超限無人知道。
核心溫度短暫超過 80°C 但當時未見裂縫，工程照常驗收；數年後筏基在地下水作用下出現不規則網狀裂縫與膨脹，修復極為困難，因為筏基上方已是整棟建築。
pitfallsEn: Treating a raft like an ordinary footing without a thermal-control plan lets the core exceed 80°C while the surface cools rapidly at night, so map or through cracks appear within days, groundwater seeps in through them, and both waterproofing and reinforcement durability suffer.

Raising cement content to secure early strength pushes the core over its limit; using high replacement without extending the design age causes 28-day strength failures and disputes; variable fly-ash batches give inconsistent heat release and strength gain.

A batch-plant breakdown or road closure suddenly cuts supply, concrete on the slope sets and new concrete cannot bond to it, leaving a large cold joint; concentrating placement at a few pump positions to catch up makes some layers too thick, so vibration is inadequate and honeycombing results.

Installing sensors only in the core leaves the differential unknown; surface sensors set too deep read high and underestimate the real differential; downloading data only during office hours means night-time exceedances go unnoticed.

A core briefly exceeds 80°C with no cracks visible at the time and the work is accepted; years later, in groundwater, the raft develops irregular map cracking and expansion that is extremely hard to repair because the whole building sits on top.

facts: Northridge 地震發生於 1994 年 1 月 17 日，規模 Mw 6.7
SAC 聯合團隊於 1994 年中由 SEAOC、ATC 與 CUREE 組成，研究計畫於 2000 年結束
Kielland 平台於 1980 年 3 月 27 日傾覆，212 人中 123 人罹難
Kielland 斜撐裂縫起於固定聲納凸緣板的 6 mm 填角焊，調查並發現層狀撕裂與冷裂
2005 年 FHWA 報告海灣大橋東段三塊鋼構試件的焊道符合或超過規範要求

factsEn: The Northridge earthquake struck on 17 January 1994 with magnitude Mw 6.7
The SAC Joint Venture was formed in mid-1994 by SEAOC, ATC and CUREE, and its program ended in 2000
The Kielland platform capsized on 27 March 1980, killing 123 of the 212 people aboard
The Kielland brace crack started at a 6 mm fillet weld holding a sonar flange plate, and the investigation also found lamellar tearing and cold cracks
In 2005 FHWA reported that welds from three Bay Bridge East Span steel pieces met or exceeded specifications
The Bay Bridge East Span self-anchored suspension bridge opened on 2 September 2013 with a tower about 160 m (525 ft) tall
Seismic demand-critical filler metals are commonly required to give 27 J (20 ft·lbf) at −29°C (−20°F) and 54 J (40 ft·lbf) at 21°C (70°F)
AWS D1.1 requires final visual inspection of quenched-and-tempered high-strength steels no sooner than 48 hours after welding

timelineEn: 1980 — The Alexander L. Kielland platform capsizes after a fatigue crack grows from an attachment fillet weld
1994 — The Northridge earthquake exposes brittle fractures in welded steel moment-frame joints, and the SAC Joint Venture is formed

2021 — The I-40 Hernando de Soto Bridge tie girder fractures, traced to fabrication weld repairs and hydrogen cracks

guides.title: 傳力、算例與驗證：鋼構巨型接頭焊接檢驗
guides.titleEn: Load paths, calculations and verification: Welding inspection of major steel joints
guides.concept: 從巨型梁柱接頭與箱型柱續接的傳力出發，說明 1994 年 Northridge 地震焊接接頭脆斷的教訓、厚板層狀撕裂與氫致冷裂、焊接程序與銲工資格、焊接順序與收縮、品管與品保停留點、超音波檢測幾何、尺寸目視檢查、缺陷修補與焊道紀錄，並以 Alexander L. Kielland 平台、I-40 Hernando de Soto 橋與舊金山—奧克蘭海灣大橋東段為實例。
guides.conceptEn: Starting from force transfer in mega beam–column joints and box-column splices, explain the lessons of brittle weld fractures in the 1994 Northridge earthquake, lamellar tearing and hydrogen cold cracking in thick plate, welding procedures and welder qualification, weld sequence and shrinkage, quality-control and quality-assurance hold points, ultrasonic testing geometry, dimensional visual inspection, defect repair and weld records, with the Alexander L. Kielland platform, the I-40 Hernando de Soto Bridge and the San Francisco–Oakland Bay Bridge East Span as examples.
procedure: 巨型梁柱接頭、桁架節點與箱型柱續接中，彎矩大多以翼板拉壓力偶傳遞，受拉翼板的全滲透開槽焊必須發揮與母材相同的強度；腹板與加勁板的填角焊則主要承受剪力。焊縫的重要性不只取決於尺寸，而取決於失效後果：位於耐震系統塑性區、承受反覆拉力或疲勞的焊縫，會被歸為需求關鍵焊縫，適用更嚴格的韌性、檢驗與紀錄要求。檢驗計畫因此要先把每一道焊縫分類，而不是一律同樣對待。

1994 年 1 月 17 日規模 6.7 的 Northridge 地震後，工程師在多棟鋼造抗彎矩構架建築中發現梁柱焊接接頭脆性斷裂，SEAOC、ATC 與 CUREE 同年組成 SAC 聯合團隊，在 FEMA 與加州緊急服務辦公室資助下研究至 2000 年。常見問題包括：留在原處的背墊板與未熔合根部形成類似裂縫的缺口，焊材韌性不足，焊接扇形孔幾何造成應力集中，以及檢驗難以看到下翼板根部。之後的規範要求需求關鍵焊縫使用有韌性保證的焊材、移除背墊板並清根補焊或加填角焊。

巨型接頭常用 50 mm 以上的厚板，焊縫收縮會在板厚方向拉扯母材；若鋼板內有平行於表面的非金屬夾雜，就可能沿夾雜層狀撕裂。另一種危險是氫致冷裂：焊材或潮濕帶入的氫、硬化的熱影響區與高拘束應力同時存在時，裂縫可能在焊後數小時至數天才出現。對策是選用 Z 向性能保證的鋼板、使用低氫焊材並保持乾燥、依碳當量與板厚預熱並控制層間溫度。Alexander L. Kielland 平台事故調查也在相關板件中發現層狀撕裂與冷裂。
焊接程序規範（WPS）規定製程、焊材、接頭形狀、焊接位置、預熱與熱輸入等變數；它必須是規範預審合格的程序，或以程序評定紀錄（PQR）的試板經拉伸、彎曲與衝擊試驗證明可行。改變重要變數（例如焊材類別、熱輸入範圍或預熱）就需要重新評定。銲工則須以同等或更困難的位置與接頭考試合格，並維持資格有效。檢驗員的第一項工作是確認每一道焊縫都有對應的有效程序，且由合格銲工施焊。
大型全滲透焊冷卻時沿焊道橫向收縮數公釐，若接頭被周圍構件拘束，收縮變成殘餘拉應力，可能造成裂縫或使構件位置偏移。超高層箱型柱的現場續接，每一個接頭的收縮累積起來會影響樓層標高與垂直度；桁架節點多方向焊接時，焊接順序則決定變形方向。因此要以對稱、分段、由拘束大處往拘束小處的順序施焊，並在製造長度中預留收縮補償。
焊接品質主要在焊接過程中決定，完工後的非破壞檢測只能抽查結果。製造廠的品管人員負責焊前組立間隙、坡口角度、清潔與預熱，焊中逐層檢查與清根，焊後外觀與尺寸；業主委託的品保人員則獨立觀察與抽驗。2005 年舊金山—奧克蘭海灣大橋東段工程的焊接品質遭前銲工與檢驗員指控後，FHWA 委託民間檢驗單位切取鋼塊做實驗室分析，報告三塊試件的焊道符合或超過規範，這種獨立驗證正是品保的角色。
厚板全滲透焊與 T 型接頭的內部缺陷主要靠超音波檢測：斜角探頭把聲波以固定折射角送入鋼板，遇到未熔合、夾渣或裂縫就反射回來，由聲程與角度換算缺陷深度與位置，再以參考靈敏度判定是否拒收。相位陣列超音波（PAUT）以多個晶片電子控制聲束角度，一次掃描就得到斷面影像，並可留下可重新檢視的數位紀錄。焊前也要掃描母材找出可能導致層狀撕裂的分層。
目視檢查是最基本也最常被輕視的焊接檢驗：焊腳尺寸、喉厚、餘高、咬邊、焊瘤、表面氣孔與弧坑裂縫，都可以用量規、放大鏡與良好照明找出來。巨型接頭中大量的填角焊承受剪力，尺寸不足會直接降低強度；咬邊與焊瘤則在焊趾形成缺口，降低疲勞強度。Kielland 平台的 6 mm 填角焊因焊道輪廓不良而降低疲勞強度，說明非主要受力的附屬焊縫也必須被檢查。
被拒收的焊縫要以碳弧刨或研磨把缺陷完全挖除，並以磁粉或滲透檢測確認挖除乾淨，再依核准的修補程序重新預熱與施焊，最後以原檢測方法重新檢驗。修補比原焊接更困難：挖槽窄深、拘束更高，同一位置反覆修補會讓熱影響區反覆受熱而劣化。I-40 Hernando de Soto 橋 2021 年斷裂的調查即指向製造時兩處寬大的焊接修補所引發的氫致裂紋，說明修補焊縫必須與原焊縫一樣受到嚴格控制。
每一道重要焊縫都應能追溯到鋼板爐號、焊接程序、銲工、施焊日期、預熱紀錄、非破壞檢測報告與修補履歷。這些紀錄在施工期間用來找出系統性問題，例如某位銲工或某個班次的拒收率偏高；在營運期間則讓檢查人員知道哪些接頭曾經修補、哪些附屬件焊在受拉構件上。Kielland 平台與 I-40 橋的事故都顯示，製造時的焊接缺陷可能在多年後才顯現，因此交接文件要讓下一代工程師找得到這些細節。
procedureEn: In mega beam–column joints, truss nodes and box-column splices, moment travels mostly as a tension–compression couple in the flanges, and the complete-joint-penetration (CJP) groove weld on the tension flange must develop the full strength of the base metal, while fillet welds on webs and stiffeners mainly carry shear. A weld's importance depends less on its size than on the consequence of its failure: welds in the yielding zones of seismic systems or under repeated tension or fatigue are classed as demand-critical, with stricter toughness, inspection and record requirements. An inspection plan therefore starts by classifying every weld rather than treating all alike.

After the magnitude 6.7 Northridge earthquake of 17 January 1994, engineers found brittle fractures in welded beam–column joints of many steel moment-frame buildings; SEAOC, ATC and CUREE formed the SAC Joint Venture that year and, funded by FEMA and the California Office of Emergency Services, studied the problem until 2000. Common issues included backing bars left in place with unfused roots acting as crack-like notches, weld metal of low toughness, stress concentrations at weld access holes, and inspection that could hardly see the root of the bottom flange. Later codes required demand-critical welds with toughness-rated filler metal, backing removal with back-gouging and reweld, or a reinforcing fillet.

Major joints often use plates thicker than 50 mm, and weld shrinkage pulls the base metal through its thickness; non-metallic inclusions lying parallel to the surface can then cause lamellar tearing. Another danger is hydrogen cold cracking: when hydrogen from consumables or moisture, a hardened heat-affected zone and high restraint stress coincide, cracks may appear hours to days after welding. Remedies are plates with guaranteed through-thickness properties, dry low-hydrogen consumables, preheat chosen by carbon equivalent and thickness, and controlled interpass temperature. The Alexander L. Kielland investigation also found lamellar tearing and cold cracks in the plates involved.

A welding procedure specification (WPS) fixes the process, consumable, joint geometry, position, preheat and heat input; it must be prequalified by the code or proven by a procedure qualification record (PQR) whose test plates pass tension, bend and impact tests. Changing an essential variable, such as consumable class, heat-input range or preheat, requires requalification. Welders must pass tests in the same or more difficult positions and joints and keep their qualifications current. The inspector's first task is to confirm that every weld has a valid procedure and is made by a qualified welder.

Large CJP welds shrink several millimetres transversely as they cool; if surrounding members restrain the joint, the shrinkage turns into residual tensile stress that can crack the weld or pull members out of position. In supertall box-column field splices the shrinkage of every joint accumulates into floor-level and plumbness errors, and in truss nodes welded from several directions the sequence decides which way the joint distorts. Welds are therefore made symmetrically, in segments, from the most restrained toward the least restrained area, with shrinkage allowances built into fabricated lengths.

Weld quality is decided mainly during welding; NDT after completion only samples the result. The fabricator's quality-control staff check fit-up gap, bevel angle, cleanliness and preheat before welding, each pass and back-gouging during welding, and appearance and size afterwards, while the owner's quality-assurance staff observe and sample independently. In 2005, after former welders and inspectors alleged poor welding on the San Francisco–Oakland Bay Bridge East Span project, FHWA had private inspectors cut sections for laboratory analysis and reported that welds from three pieces met or exceeded specifications, an example of exactly this kind of independent assurance.

Internal flaws in thick-plate CJP welds and T-joints are found mainly by ultrasonic testing: an angle-beam probe sends sound into the plate at a fixed refracted angle, lack of fusion, slag or cracks reflect it back, and sound path and angle locate the flaw's depth and position, judged against reference sensitivity for rejection. Phased-array ultrasonics (PAUT) steer the beam electronically with many elements, producing a cross-sectional image in one scan and a digital record that can be reviewed later. Base metal near the joint is also scanned before welding to find laminations that could lead to lamellar tearing.

Visual inspection is the most basic and most often underrated weld check: leg size, throat, reinforcement, undercut, overlap, surface porosity and crater cracks can all be found with gauges, a magnifier and good lighting. Major joints contain many fillet welds carrying shear, and undersize directly reduces strength; undercut and overlap notch the weld toe and cut fatigue strength. On the Kielland platform a 6 mm fillet weld with a poor profile had reduced fatigue strength, showing that welds on non-load-bearing attachments must be inspected too.

A rejected weld is excavated by air-carbon-arc gouging or grinding until the flaw is fully removed, confirmed clean by magnetic particle or penetrant testing, then preheated and rewelded to an approved repair procedure and re-tested by the original method. Repairs are harder than original welds: the excavation is narrow and deep, restraint is higher, and repeated repairs at one spot reheat and degrade the heat-affected zone. The investigation of the 2021 I-40 Hernando de Soto Bridge fracture pointed to hydrogen cracks from two wide weld repairs made during fabrication, showing that repair welds need the same strict control as the originals.

Every important weld should trace back to plate heat number, welding procedure, welder, date, preheat record, NDT reports and repair history. During construction these records expose systematic problems, such as one welder or shift with a high reject rate; in service they tell inspectors which joints were repaired and which attachments are welded to tension members. The Kielland platform and the I-40 bridge both show that fabrication weld defects can surface years later, so handover documents must let the next generation of engineers find these details.
evidence: 結構設計者必須在圖說中明確指定需求關鍵焊縫與各焊縫的檢驗等級，不能留給製造廠判斷；焊縫清冊列為施工圖審查的必要文件，未經結構工程師核定不得開始製造。
耐震抗彎矩接頭的細部（扇形孔形狀、背墊板處理、補強填角焊）要採用經試驗驗證的接頭型式，任何現場變更都須經結構工程師核准；地震後的檢查計畫要預先指定拆除被覆的抽查接頭位置。
厚板接頭的焊接程序要明訂最低預熱、最高層間溫度、熱輸入範圍與焊材烘乾保管要求；對淬火回火等高強度鋼，最終目視與非破壞檢測應在焊後規定的等待時間（例如 48 小時）後進行。
每個焊接工作站張貼適用的 WPS 摘要，檢驗員每班至少抽測一次電流、電壓與行進速度；程序任何變更都須重新提送審查，未經核准的變更所做的焊縫一律列為不符合項目。
製造廠應提交焊接順序計畫，標示每一道焊縫的施焊順序、分段長度與銲工配置（例如對邊兩人同時施焊），並由結構工程師審查；現場不得因方便而改變順序，變更須重新核准。
evidenceEn: The structural designer must specify demand-critical welds and the inspection level of every weld on the drawings rather than leave it to the fabricator; the weld register is a required submittal in shop-drawing review, and fabrication may not start before the structural engineer approves it.

Seismic moment-connection details (access-hole shape, backing treatment, reinforcing fillets) must follow test-qualified connection types, and any field change needs the structural engineer's approval; post-earthquake inspection plans should name in advance which joints will have fireproofing removed for checks.

Thick-plate procedures must state minimum preheat, maximum interpass temperature, heat-input range and consumable drying and storage; for quenched-and-tempered high-strength steels, final visual inspection and NDT should follow a specified waiting time after welding, such as 48 hours.

Post the applicable WPS summary at every welding station and have the inspector check current, voltage and travel speed at least once per shift; any procedure change must be resubmitted for review, and welds made under an unapproved change are recorded as nonconformances.

The fabricator should submit a weld-sequence plan showing the order, segment lengths and welder arrangement for every weld (for example two welders working opposite faces at once), reviewed by the structural engineer; the sequence may not be changed on site for convenience without re-approval.
pitfalls: 若施工圖把受拉翼板全滲透焊誤標為一般焊縫，只做目視檢查，內部未熔合或夾渣就會留在接頭中，在地震或強風的大拉力下由缺陷處脆性斷裂，裂縫可能貫穿翼板並延伸到柱翼板。
在冬季未預熱就焊接厚板，或焊條暴露在潮濕空氣中過久，焊後隔天才在熱影響區出現細微裂縫；若在完工當下就做完非破壞檢測並放行，這些延遲裂縫會被包覆在防火被覆或混凝土內。
若四面箱型柱同時由一側焊完再焊另一側，柱段會向先焊的一側傾斜；拘束很高的節點一次焊滿而不分段，冷卻時在焊根或熱影響區產生橫向裂縫，往往要到超音波檢測才發現。
若只從一側以單一角度掃描，平行於聲束的平面型未熔合可能完全不反射而被漏判；耦合劑不足或表面有焊濺物，也會使靈敏度下降，讓應拒收的缺陷看起來可以接受。
修補時未完全挖除裂縫末端，或為了快速完成而省略預熱，新焊道下方留下氫致裂紋；這類裂縫可能多年後才在使用應力下成長並造成斷裂。
pitfallsEn: If shop drawings mislabel a tension-flange CJP weld as an ordinary weld inspected only visually, internal lack of fusion or slag stays in the joint and, under large seismic or wind tension, starts a brittle fracture that can run through the flange into the column flange.

Welding thick plate in winter without preheat, or with electrodes left too long in damp air, lets fine cracks appear in the heat-affected zone a day later; if NDT is done immediately and the joint released, these delayed cracks are sealed inside fireproofing or concrete.

Welding one face of a four-sided box column completely before the opposite face tilts the segment toward the first side; filling a highly restrained node in one go without segmenting can crack the root or heat-affected zone transversely on cooling, often found only by ultrasonic testing.

Scanning from one side at a single angle can miss a planar lack-of-fusion flaw lying parallel to the beam, which returns no echo; poor couplant or weld spatter on the surface lowers sensitivity so that a rejectable flaw looks acceptable.
Leaving the tip of a crack unexcavated, or skipping preheat to finish quickly, leaves hydrogen cracks beneath the new weld that may grow under service stress and fracture years later.

guides.concept: 以夾緊力、接觸面等級、預拉方法與安裝前驗證，確保摩擦型與預拉接頭在施工及數十年使用中保持設計夾緊力。數據取自公開資料並經四捨五入，用於學習比較，不是設計值。

facts: RCSC 第一版高強度螺栓接頭規範於 1951 年 1 月發布，至今共 18 個後續版本
RCSC 2025 年版撤除校正扳手法（第 7.2、8.2、9.2 節）
RCSC 接觸面 Class A 平均滑動係數至少 0.30，Class B 為 0.50，設計不得採用大於 0.50 的值
7/8 in 螺栓最低預拉力為最低抗拉強度的 70%：A325 約 39 kips（173 kN）、A490 約 49 kips（218 kN）
轉角法常見規定：螺栓長度不超過 4 倍直徑轉 1/3 圈，4 至 8 倍轉 1/2 圈，8 至 12 倍轉 2/3 圈
雪梨港灣大橋約有 600 萬支手工鉚釘，最大一支重 3.5 kg、長 39.5 cm
海灣大橋東段 288 支直徑 3 in、長 9 至 17 ft 的錨桿中，最先受拉的 96 支有 32 支在兩週內斷裂
Kemper Arena 屋頂於 1979 年 6 月 4 日在約 70 mph 強風與大雨中倒塌約 200×215 ft
factsEn: RCSC published its first high-strength bolted-joint specification in January 1951 and has issued 18 successive editions since
The 2025 RCSC Specification withdrew the calibrated wrench method (Sections 7.2, 8.2 and 9.2)
RCSC Class A faying surfaces have a mean slip coefficient of at least 0.30 and Class B 0.50, and no design value above 0.50 may be used
Minimum pretension for 7/8 in bolts is 70% of minimum tensile strength: about 39 kips (173 kN) for A325 and 49 kips (218 kN) for A490
Common turn-of-nut rules: 1/3 turn for lengths up to 4 diameters, 1/2 turn for 4 to 8, and 2/3 turn for 8 to 12
Sydney Harbour Bridge has about 6 million hand-driven rivets, the largest weighing 3.5 kg and 39.5 cm long
Of the Bay Bridge East Span's 288 three-inch anchor rods, 9 to 17 ft long, 32 of the first 96 tensioned broke within two weeks
About 200×215 ft of the Kemper Arena roof collapsed on 4 June 1979 in winds of about 70 mph and heavy rain
timeline: 1932　雪梨港灣大橋以約六百萬支手工鉚釘建成通車，代表鉚接時代的大型鋼構
1951　RCSC 發布第一版高強度螺栓接頭規範，預拉螺栓開始取代鉚釘
1979　Kemper Arena 屋頂吊架螺栓在風雨中失效，引發大面積屋頂倒塌
2013　海灣大橋東段高強度錨桿受拉後大量斷裂，以加裝鞍座補強後於 12 月啟用
2025　RCSC 新版規範撤除校正扳手法，並新增螺栓施工人員資格條文
timelineEn: 1932 — Sydney Harbour Bridge opens, built with about six million hand-driven rivets, emblematic of the riveted era
1951 — RCSC publishes its first high-strength bolted-joint specification, and pretensioned bolts begin to replace rivets
1979 — Kemper Arena's roof hanger bolts fail in a storm, triggering a large roof collapse
2013 — Many high-strength anchor rods on the Bay Bridge East Span break after tensioning; a saddle retrofit enters service in December
2025 — The new RCSC Specification withdraws the calibrated wrench method and adds bolting personnel qualification provisions

guides.title: 傳力、算例與驗證：高強度螺栓預拉力施工
guides.titleEn: Load paths, calculations and verification: Pretensioning of high-strength structural bolts
guides.concept: 從摩擦型接頭的傳力與預拉力對疲勞的作用出發，說明螺栓等級與氫脆、接觸面處理與孔型、密貼與鎖緊順序、轉角法、扭剪型螺栓與直接張力指示墊圈、安裝前驗證與施工後稽核、長期鬆弛與紀錄交接，並以 RCSC 規範 2025 年版撤除校正扳手法、舊金山—奧克蘭海灣大橋 2013 年錨桿斷裂、1979 年 Kemper Arena 屋頂吊架螺栓失效與雪梨港灣大橋六百萬支鉚釘為對照。
guides.conceptEn: Starting from force transfer in slip-critical joints and the role of pretension in fatigue, explain bolt grades and hydrogen embrittlement, faying surfaces and hole types, snugging and tightening sequence, turn-of-nut, twist-off bolts and direct tension indicators, pre-installation verification and post-installation audits, long-term relaxation and record handover, contrasted with the withdrawal of the calibrated wrench method in the 2025 RCSC Specification, the 2013 anchor-rod fractures on the San Francisco–Oakland Bay Bridge, the 1979 Kemper Arena hanger-bolt failure and the six million rivets of Sydney Harbour Bridge.
procedure: 高強度螺栓接頭有兩種傳力方式：承壓型接頭讓板件滑動到螺栓桿與孔壁接觸，以螺栓剪力與孔壁承壓傳力；摩擦型接頭則靠螺栓預拉力把板件夾緊，以接觸面的摩擦力傳遞剪力，在使用載重下板件不滑動。需要摩擦型接頭的情況包括反覆或反向載重、疲勞敏感構件、超大孔或槽孔，以及滑動會造成幾何改變的支撐與續接。摩擦型接頭的強度因此直接取決於夾緊力與接觸面滑動係數，而不是螺栓本身的剪力強度。

受拉接頭中的預拉力讓螺栓與被夾板件形成預壓的彈簧系統：外加拉力大部分只是減少板件間的壓力，螺栓本身只多承受一小部分，因此應力變化小、疲勞壽命長；但一旦外力超過分離載重，板件張開，螺栓承受全部外力並可能出現撬力。1979 年 6 月 4 日 Kansas City 的 Kemper Arena 在約 70 mph 強風與大雨中，屋頂吊架螺栓的強度被低估、積水又增加載重，一支螺栓失效後引發連鎖破壞，約 200×215 ft 的屋頂倒塌。

結構用高強度螺栓依 ASTM F3125 分為 A325（最低抗拉 120 ksi，約 830 MPa）與 A490（150 ksi，約 1,040 MPa）等級，以及對應的扭剪型螺栓；螺帽與墊圈須搭配相容等級。強度越高的鋼對氫脆越敏感：酸洗、電鍍或熱浸鍍鋅帶入的氫，加上持續高拉應力，可能在鎖緊後數天內造成延遲斷裂，因此 A490 等級不得熱浸鍍鋅。2013 年舊金山—奧克蘭海灣大橋東段 288 支直徑 3 in 的錨桿中，最先受拉的 96 支在兩週內有 32 支斷裂，起初即被歸因於氫脆。

摩擦型接頭的滑動係數取決於接觸面：RCSC 規範把清潔的軋鋼皮面歸為 Class A，平均滑動係數至少 0.30，噴砂清理面歸為 Class B，設計值為 0.50，且設計不得採用大於 0.50 的值；塗裝接觸面必須依附錄的滑動試驗取得等級，鍍鋅接觸面在設計上視為 Class A。孔型也影響抗滑：超大孔與槽孔讓夾緊區域減少、對位誤差增大，須折減強度。接觸面範圍內的油漆噴濺、油污與毛邊都會顯著降低摩擦。
預拉之前，接頭必須先達到密貼：所有板件緊密接觸，通常由鐵工以一般扳手全力鎖緊或衝擊扳手數次衝擊達成。鎖緊要從接頭最剛硬的部分（通常是中央）往自由邊系統化推進，因為後鎖的螺栓會把板件進一步拉近，使先鎖的螺栓夾緊力下降。板件較厚、層數較多或板面不平時，往往需要多輪鎖緊，才能讓每一支螺栓在最後都達到最低預拉力。

預拉方法的核心是用可檢查的量取代不可靠的扭力：轉角法在密貼後把螺帽相對螺栓轉過規定角度，以應變控制使螺栓進入非彈性範圍，預拉力穩定；扭剪型螺栓在尾端花鍵被扳手扭斷時達到張力；直接張力指示墊圈的凸點被壓扁到規定間隙，以塞尺判定；另有合併法。RCSC 2025 年版規範撤除了校正扳手法，因為扭力與張力的關係受潤滑、螺紋狀態與溫度影響很大。轉角量依螺栓長度與直徑比而定，例如長度不超過 4 倍直徑時為 1/3 圈。
任何預拉方法在現場使用前，都要以同批的螺栓、螺帽與墊圈組件，在液壓式螺栓張力校正器中照實際程序鎖緊，量測得到的張力，確認方法、工具與組件組合能達到規定的最低預拉力並留有餘裕（一般要求至少 1.05 倍）。這項試驗能抓出潤滑不足、批次不符、工具設定錯誤或螺栓太短無法裝入校正器等問題；RCSC 2025 年版另新增了驗證不合格時的處理程序。驗證要在每一批、每一種直徑與長度組合開工時進行。
預拉螺栓完成後無法直接看出張力，因此檢驗重點在於觀察過程：檢驗員觀察安裝前驗證，並定期觀察鐵工是否依程序密貼、標記與鎖緊，最後檢查轉角標記、扭斷尾端或指示墊圈間隙。若對已安裝螺栓有疑問，可用稽查扭力法：先以同批組件在校正器中求出達到規定張力所需的扭力，再以校正過的扭力扳手檢查現場螺栓是否在該扭力下不再轉動；RCSC 2025 年版新增稽查用扭力扳手的校正要求。
預拉力在使用期間會因為幾個原因下降：螺紋與承壓面的局部嵌入、接觸面厚塗層的潛變、鍍鋅層的蠕變、腐蝕減少有效截面，以及反覆振動造成的鬆動。由於螺栓的軸向勁度很高，被夾區域只要縮短百分之幾毫米，夾緊力就明顯下降。高強度螺栓還可能因環境氫或腐蝕反應而延遲斷裂。維護時常見的問題是是否可以重新鎖緊：A490 與鍍鋅的 A325 螺栓不得重複使用，鬆動的螺栓通常應更換而非直接回鎖。
鉚接時代的接頭一旦完成就幾乎無法調整，雪梨港灣大橋以約六百萬支手工鉚釘接合，最大的一支重 3.5 kg、長 39.5 cm；高強度螺栓接頭則可以檢查、更換與重新預拉，但前提是紀錄完整。交接文件要讓維護人員知道：哪些接頭是摩擦型或預拉型、使用哪個等級與批號、採用何種預拉方法、安裝前驗證與稽核結果、曾經有哪些不符合項目與更換。沒有這些紀錄，任何一支斷裂螺栓都無法判斷是單一事件還是整批問題。
procedureEn: High-strength bolted joints transfer force in two ways: in a bearing joint the plies slip until the shank bears on the hole, carrying force by bolt shear and bearing; in a slip-critical joint the bolt pretension clamps the plies so friction at the faying surfaces carries the shear without slip under service loads. Slip-critical joints are needed for reversing or repeated loads, fatigue-sensitive members, oversized or slotted holes, and bracing or splices where slip would change geometry. Their capacity therefore depends directly on clamp force and the faying-surface slip coefficient, not on the shear strength of the bolt itself.

Pretension turns a tension joint into a preloaded spring system of bolt and clamped plies: most of an applied tension only reduces the contact pressure between plies, and the bolt picks up only a small share, so its stress range stays small and fatigue life long; once the load exceeds the separation load, the plies open, the bolt takes the whole load and prying can appear. At Kemper Arena in Kansas City on 4 June 1979, in winds of about 70 mph and heavy rain, the strength of the roof hanger bolts had been underestimated and ponding added load; one bolt gave way, starting a cascade that dropped a roof area of about 200×215 ft.

Structural high-strength bolts under ASTM F3125 include Grade A325 (minimum tensile 120 ksi, about 830 MPa) and A490 (150 ksi, about 1,040 MPa) with matching twist-off versions, and nuts and washers must be of compatible grades. Higher-strength steel is more sensitive to hydrogen embrittlement: hydrogen from pickling, electroplating or hot-dip galvanizing, combined with sustained high tension, can cause delayed fracture within days of tightening, which is why Grade A490 must not be hot-dip galvanized. In 2013, of the 288 three-inch anchor rods on the San Francisco–Oakland Bay Bridge East Span, 32 of the first 96 to be tensioned broke within two weeks, a failure initially attributed to hydrogen embrittlement.

The slip coefficient of a slip-critical joint depends on the faying surface: the RCSC Specification treats clean mill scale as Class A with a mean slip coefficient of at least 0.30 and blast-cleaned steel as Class B with a design value of 0.50, and no design value above 0.50 may be used; coated faying surfaces must earn their class by slip testing per the appendix, and galvanized faying surfaces count as Class A for design. Hole type also matters: oversized and slotted holes reduce the clamped area and allow misalignment, so strength is reduced. Paint overspray, oil and burrs within the faying area cut friction markedly.

Before pretensioning, a joint must be snug: all plies in firm contact, usually achieved by an ironworker's full effort on an ordinary spanner or a few impacts of an impact wrench. Tightening must progress systematically from the most rigid part of the joint, usually the centre, toward the free edges, because later bolts pull the plies closer and reduce the clamp on bolts tightened earlier. Thick plates, many plies or uneven surfaces often require several passes before every bolt finally reaches minimum pretension.

Pretensioning methods replace unreliable torque with checkable quantities: turn-of-nut rotates the nut a specified angle relative to the bolt after snugging, using strain control to push the bolt into the inelastic range for consistent pretension; twist-off tension-control bolts reach tension when the spline end shears off; direct tension indicators have protrusions that flatten to a specified gap judged with a feeler gauge; and a combined method also exists. The 2025 RCSC Specification withdrew the calibrated wrench method, because the torque–tension relation varies greatly with lubrication, thread condition and temperature. Turn-of-nut rotation depends on bolt length relative to diameter, for example 1/3 turn when the length is no more than four diameters.

Before any pretensioning method is used in the field, assemblies of bolts, nuts and washers from the same lots are tightened by the actual procedure in a hydraulic bolt tension calibrator and the tension measured, confirming that method, tools and assemblies reach the specified minimum pretension with margin, typically at least 1.05 times. The test catches poor lubrication, mismatched lots, wrong tool settings, or bolts too short to fit the calibrator; the 2025 RCSC edition also adds procedures for nonconforming verification tests. Verification is done at the start of work for every lot and every diameter and length combination.

Because pretension cannot be seen once a bolt is installed, inspection focuses on observing the process: the inspector witnesses pre-installation verification, periodically watches crews snug, mark and tighten by procedure, and finally checks match marks, sheared splines or indicator gaps. Where installed bolts are in dispute, arbitration torque is used: the torque needed to reach specified tension is found for same-lot assemblies in the calibrator, then a calibrated torque wrench checks whether field bolts resist turning at that torque; the 2025 RCSC edition adds calibration requirements for the arbitration torque wrench.

Pretension declines in service for several reasons: local embedment at threads and bearing faces, creep of thick coatings on faying surfaces, creep of galvanized layers, corrosion reducing the effective section, and loosening under repeated vibration. Because a bolt is axially very stiff, the clamped zone need only shorten by hundredths of a millimetre for clamp force to drop noticeably. High-strength bolts may also suffer delayed fracture from environmental hydrogen or corrosion reactions. A common maintenance question is whether bolts may be retightened: A490 and galvanized A325 bolts must not be reused, and loose bolts are usually replaced rather than simply retightened.

Riveted joints were practically unadjustable once made, and Sydney Harbour Bridge is held together by about six million hand-driven rivets, the largest weighing 3.5 kg and 39.5 cm long; high-strength bolted joints can be inspected, replaced and re-pretensioned, but only if the records are complete. Handover documents must tell maintainers which joints are slip-critical or pretensioned, which grade and lot was used, which pretensioning method, the verification and audit results, and any nonconformances and replacements. Without these records, nobody can tell whether a broken bolt is an isolated event or a lot-wide problem.
evidence: 結構設計者應在圖說中明確指定哪些接頭必須是摩擦型及其接觸面等級，製造廠的塗裝計畫要以遮蔽標示接觸面範圍；任何接觸面塗層變更都須提出滑動係數試驗證明並經核准。
吊掛屋頂、懸吊樓板或設備吊架等受拉關鍵接頭，應以冗餘設計使單一螺栓失效不致連鎖倒塌，並指定為預拉接頭且列入定期檢查清單；設計者須在計算書中寫明分離載重與撬力檢核。
規格書要寫明螺栓、螺帽與墊圈的標準與等級、表面處理限制（例如 A490 禁止熱浸鍍鋅）與批號追溯要求；現場不同批次與等級的螺栓須分區存放並保持潤滑與乾燥，未標示的螺栓不得使用。
接觸面在製造廠就以遮蔽膠帶標示並在施工圖註明「接觸面勿塗」，現場組立前由檢驗員簽認接觸面狀態；運輸與吊裝時以覆蓋保護接觸面，受污染者須重新清理至規定等級。
安裝程序應規定密貼與預拉為兩個分開的階段，並把接頭密貼後的檢查列為停留點；厚板或多層板接頭的鎖緊輪數與順序應在首件安裝時以張力量測確認，再推廣到其餘接頭。
evidenceEn: The structural designer must state which joints are slip-critical and their faying-surface class, and the fabricator's painting plan must mask and mark faying areas; any change of faying-surface coating needs slip-coefficient test evidence and approval.

Tension-critical joints such as hung roofs, suspended floors or equipment hangers should be redundant so one bolt failure cannot cascade, specified as pretensioned and placed on the periodic inspection list; the designer must record the separation-load and prying checks in the calculations.

The specification must name standards and grades for bolts, nuts and washers, coating limits (for example no hot-dip galvanizing of A490) and lot traceability; on site, different lots and grades are stored separately, kept lubricated and dry, and unmarked bolts are never used.

Mask faying areas at the shop and mark the shop drawings with a do-not-paint note, and have the inspector sign off faying-surface condition before field fit-up; protect faying areas with covers during shipping and erection, and re-clean any contaminated area to the specified class.

The installation procedure should treat snugging and pretensioning as separate stages with a hold point after snugging; for thick or multi-ply joints, confirm the number of passes and sequence on the first joint by tension measurement before applying it to the rest.
pitfalls: 若摩擦型接頭的接觸面被誤塗面漆，或預拉力不足，接頭在使用載重下滑動，支撐構架因螺栓孔間隙而鬆動，反覆載重下孔壁磨損、螺栓承受未設計的反覆剪力，最終產生疲勞裂縫或連接鬆脫。
把 A490 螺栓送去熱浸鍍鋅，或在高硬度螺栓上使用電鍍後未除氫，鎖緊後數天在螺紋根部或頭下圓角突然斷裂，斷口平整且無明顯塑性變形；海灣大橋錨桿最後以加裝鞍座的方式補強，2013 年 12 月 19 日正式啟用。
厚板接頭未先全面密貼就直接逐支鎖到最終預拉，先鎖的螺栓在後續鎖緊中被放鬆，接頭中央夾緊力不足；若是轉角法，鬆動後的螺栓已經轉過規定角度，標記看似合格，實際預拉力卻不足。
若省略安裝前驗證，某批扭剪型螺栓因螺帽潤滑不足，在尾端扭斷時張力只有規定值的七到八成，整座建築數千支螺栓都不足，直到事後抽查才發現，補救需要逐支更換。
在接觸面使用未經滑動與潛變試驗的厚塗層，接頭完工時預拉力合格，數年後夾緊力流失，摩擦型接頭在強風或地震時滑動；海邊環境的螺栓頭與螺紋腐蝕，也可能在檢查前就失去大部分截面。
pitfallsEn: If a slip-critical faying surface is painted by mistake or pretension is short, the joint slips under service load, bracing loosens through the hole clearances, and repeated loading wears the holes and subjects bolts to unintended cyclic shear, ending in fatigue cracks or a loose connection.

Hot-dip galvanizing A490 bolts, or electroplating hard bolts without hydrogen relief, leads to sudden fractures at the thread root or under-head fillet days after tightening, with flat faces and little plastic deformation; the Bay Bridge rods were ultimately bypassed by added saddle assemblies, placed in service on 19 December 2013.

Taking bolts in a thick-plate joint one by one to final pretension without first snugging the whole joint loosens the early bolts as later ones are tightened, leaving the joint centre under-clamped; with turn-of-nut, those relaxed bolts have already turned the required angle, so their marks look right while their pretension is short.

Skipping verification can let a lot of twist-off bolts with dry nuts shear at only seventy to eighty percent of required tension, leaving thousands of bolts across a building short until an after-the-fact audit finds them, with bolt-by-bolt replacement as the remedy.

Using a thick faying coating never tested for slip and creep leaves pretension correct at completion but lost within a few years, so the slip-critical joint slips in a storm or earthquake; in a marine setting, corrosion of bolt heads and threads can remove most of the section before anyone inspects it.

guides.scopeEn: Original teaching built from public engineering principles, official sources and code frameworks. Steps are verifiable learning tasks and hypothetical exercises, not design drawings, method statements, lifting or stressing permits, or any project's design documents. Numbers are teaching assumptions or public data; real work must be recalculated and certified by qualified engineers using codes and measured data.

1985 — Structural drawings for 7 World Trade Center are issued, with floor beams made composite by shear studs
2001 — 7 World Trade Center collapses after prolonged fires, making thermal expansion of composite floors a focus of investigation
2004 — Eurocode EN 1994-1-1 is published, including design rules for shear connection and push-out testing
2008 — NIST issues its final report on 7 World Trade Center, recommending evaluation of thermal expansion in composite floors and connections

沿著工程時間軸，標出設計、施工、事件與維護改造的關鍵決策點，說明每個決策改變了哪一條傳力路徑或檢核。

從代表工程中選一個與本課比較，列出跨度或高度、結構系統、主要荷載與施工方法的差異。
procedureEn: Compare the key figures with this course's worked example and mark which are public project data and which are teaching assumptions.
Along the timeline, mark the key design, construction, event and retrofit decisions and say which load path or check each one changed.
Against the listed codes and standards, find the kind of clause behind this course's tests or acceptance steps, noting edition and jurisdiction.
Pick one landmark project to compare with this course and list differences in span or height, structural system, main loads and construction method.

Applying another country's clauses without checking edition, jurisdiction and load combinations.

guides.title: 傳力、算例與驗證：組合樓板剪力釘焊接
guides.titleEn: Load paths, calculations and verification: Stud welding for composite floor systems
guides.concept: 從組合梁介面的水平剪力流與部分組合出發，說明頭釘強度與壓型鋼板肋的折減、穿板焊接的電流與環境條件、首件 30° 彎曲試驗與外觀檢查、推出試驗求取剪力釘強度，以及火災溫度效應與改修時的紀錄需求，並以 NIST 對世界貿易中心七號樓組合樓板的調查、雙子塔以桁架「指節」取得組合作用的樓板，以及英國鋼結構協會對穿板焊接的說明為依據。
guides.conceptEn: Starting from horizontal shear flow and partial composite action at the beam–slab interface, explain headed-stud strength and its reduction in deck ribs, current and site conditions for through-deck welding, first-stud 30° bend tests and visual checks, push-out tests for stud resistance, and fire and thermal effects and record-keeping for alterations, drawing on NIST's investigation of the composite floors of 7 World Trade Center, the Twin Towers' floors made composite by truss knuckles, and steel-industry guidance on through-deck welding.
procedure: 鋼梁上的混凝土樓板若只是放在梁上，兩者各自彎曲，接觸面會相對滑動；焊在上翼板的剪力釘阻止滑動，讓樓板成為受壓翼緣、鋼梁成為受拉部分，斷面像一根更深的梁，強度與勁度都大幅提高。剪力釘要傳遞的是從零彎矩點到最大彎矩點之間的水平剪力總和，等於混凝土受壓合力與鋼梁受拉合力中較小者。剪力釘數量不足時，梁只能部分組合，強度與勁度介於純鋼梁與完全組合之間。
實務上很多組合梁刻意設計成部分組合，因為壓型鋼板肋距限制了可焊剪力釘的位置，而強度往往不需要完全組合。部分組合時，介面有少量滑動，有效慣性矩低於完全組合的換算斷面，撓度與樓板振動因此變大。組合比（實際剪力釘總強度除以完全組合所需值）同時控制強度與勁度，太低時剪力釘會在變形能力用盡前斷裂，因此規範通常設定最低組合比。
建築組合樓板最常用的是直徑 19 mm 的頭釘，釘頭讓混凝土能抵抗拔出，釘身則以剪力與彎曲把介面力傳入混凝土。單支剪力釘的強度由兩個機制中較小者決定：周圍混凝土被壓碎或劈裂，或釘身鋼材剪斷；放在壓型鋼板肋內時，肋的寬度、高度與剪力釘在肋中的位置還會進一步折減強度，例如剪力釘位於受力方向的不利側（弱位置）時強度明顯較低。
英國鋼結構業界的說明指出，穿板焊接是把剪力釘固定在鋼梁上翼板的常規做法：壓型鋼板夾在剪力釘底部與翼板之間，一次焊接把三者熔合。約 1 mm 厚的鍍鋅鋼承板不影響焊接品質，但鋼承板必須緊貼翼板、保持乾燥，翼板頂面不得有影響焊接的厚塗層。橫向鋪設的鋼承板每個肋內通常最多兩支剪力釘，因此肋距直接決定可配置的剪力釘數量；兩支並排時每支強度又會再折減。
拉弧式剪力釘焊接由焊槍提起剪力釘引弧，在設定時間內熔化釘端與母材，再把剪力釘壓入熔池；釘端的鋁球協助脫氧，陶瓷護圈集中熱量、保護熔池並使焊瘤成形，焊後敲除。焊接品質取決於電流、時間、提升與壓入量的組合，而這些設定又受剪力釘直徑、是否穿板、焊接電纜長度與接地位置影響。現場常見問題是電源容量不足、電纜過長或接地不良，使實際電流低於設定。
每個生產時段開始或設定改變時，先在代表性的構件上焊兩支剪力釘，目視確認 360° 完整焊瘤，再用鐵鎚把剪力釘敲彎約 30°，焊道與熱影響區不得斷裂；通過後才開始量產。焊後長度也要檢查：拉弧焊接會消耗數公釐長度，焊後剪力釘必須高出鋼承板頂足夠距離，頂端又要保留足夠的混凝土保護層，兩者都影響剪力釘的錨定與耐久。
量產中的剪力釘檢查以全數目視為主：焊瘤應完整環繞釘根，沒有缺口、裂紋或過度飛濺；剪力釘應垂直、長度一致。焊瘤不完整或可疑的剪力釘可以鐵鎚敲擊聽聲，或敲彎約 15° 檢查根部，不合格者須在旁邊補焊新剪力釘或依程序以填角焊修補。由於混凝土澆置後無法再檢查，檢驗必須在澆置前完成並放行，這是整個組合樓板最關鍵的停留點。
剪力釘在特定壓型鋼板、混凝土與焊接條件下的強度與滑移能力，可用推出試驗直接量測：把焊有剪力釘的短鋼梁夾在兩塊混凝土板之間，從上方推壓鋼梁，記錄載重與滑移，直到剪力釘或混凝土破壞。歐洲規範 EN 1994-1-1 以特徵滑移能力至少 6 mm 作為延性剪力釘的條件，並提供由試驗結果求取設計強度的方法。新型壓型鋼板、特殊剪力釘或非標準焊接條件，都應以推出試驗確認。

剪力釘讓鋼梁與樓板連成一體，這在常溫下是優點，在火災中卻會帶來另一種力：受熱的組合梁膨脹時被周圍結構束制，產生很大的軸向推力，推向梁端接頭與相鄰大梁。NIST 對世界貿易中心七號樓的調查指出，樓板梁以剪力釘與混凝土組合，長跨樓板梁在遠低於一般設計考慮的溫度下熱膨脹，推動一根關鍵大梁離開其在 79 號柱的支承座，引發樓板連續破壞與柱挫屈；NIST 建議設計時檢討組合樓板與未考慮熱效應之接頭的熱膨脹影響。
樓板完成後剪力釘全部埋在混凝土中，日後改修時工程師只能依賴紀錄判斷樓板與梁的組合程度。不同年代的組合樓板做法也不同：NIST 描述世界貿易中心雙子塔的樓板以輕型鋼桁架支承 4 in 厚的輕質混凝土，桁架腹桿頂端彎折的「指節」伸出上弦約 3 in 埋入樓板而產生組合作用，而不是焊接剪力釘。改修時若在梁旁開大洞、切除樓板或增加重載設備，都可能減少有效的剪力連接，必須依原始紀錄重新檢核。
procedureEn: A concrete slab merely resting on a steel beam bends separately and slips along the interface; studs welded to the top flange prevent this slip so the slab becomes a compression flange and the steel a tension zone, behaving like a much deeper beam with far greater strength and stiffness. The studs must carry the total horizontal shear between the points of zero and maximum moment, equal to the smaller of the concrete compression force and the steel tension force. With too few studs, the beam is only partially composite, with strength and stiffness between those of the bare steel and full composite action.

In practice many composite beams are deliberately partially composite, because deck rib spacing limits where studs can go and strength often does not need full composite action. With partial composite action the interface slips slightly and the effective moment of inertia falls below that of the fully composite transformed section, so deflection and floor vibration increase. The composite ratio, total stud strength divided by that required for full action, governs both strength and stiffness; too low a ratio lets studs fracture before their deformation capacity is used, so codes usually set a minimum ratio.

The most common connector in building composite floors is the 19 mm headed stud: the head anchors it against pull-out while the shank carries interface force into the concrete by shear and bending. A single stud's resistance is the lesser of two mechanisms, crushing or splitting of the surrounding concrete or shearing of the steel shank; inside a deck rib, the rib's width and height and the stud's position within it reduce strength further, notably when the stud sits on the unfavourable side of the rib relative to the load, the weak position.

Steel-industry guidance in the UK describes through-deck welding as the normal way to fix studs to a beam's top flange: the decking is sandwiched between the stud base and the flange and one weld fuses all three. Galvanized decking about 1 mm thick does not affect weld quality, but the deck must sit tight on the flange and be dry, and the flange top must be free of thick coatings that impair welding. With transverse decking, usually no more than two studs go in one trough, so rib spacing directly sets how many studs can be placed, and two studs side by side are each reduced further.

In drawn-arc stud welding the gun lifts the stud to strike an arc, melts the stud end and base metal for a set time, then plunges the stud into the pool; an aluminium flux ball on the stud end deoxidises the weld, and a ceramic ferrule concentrates heat, shields the pool and shapes the flash before being knocked off. Quality depends on the combination of current, time, lift and plunge, which in turn depend on stud diameter, whether welding through deck, cable length and ground position. Common site problems are undersized power supplies, overlong cables and poor grounds that leave actual current below the setting.

At the start of each production period or after a settings change, two studs are welded on a representative member, checked visually for a full 360° flash, then hammered over to about 30°; neither weld nor heat-affected zone may fracture, and only then does production begin. After-weld length is checked too: the drawn-arc process consumes a few millimetres, and the welded stud must still project far enough above the deck while leaving enough concrete cover over its head, both affecting anchorage and durability.

Production studs are checked mainly by 100% visual inspection: the flash should fully encircle the base with no gaps, cracks or excessive spatter, and studs should be upright and of consistent length. Studs with incomplete or doubtful flash can be ring-tested with a hammer or bent about 15° to check the base, and rejects are replaced by a new stud alongside or repaired by fillet welding per the procedure. Because nothing can be checked once concrete is placed, inspection must be completed and released before casting, the single most critical hold point for a composite floor.

The strength and slip capacity of studs with a particular deck, concrete and welding condition can be measured directly by push-out tests: a short steel section with studs is sandwiched between two concrete slabs and pushed down while load and slip are recorded until the studs or concrete fail. EN 1994-1-1 treats studs as ductile when their characteristic slip capacity is at least 6 mm and gives a procedure for deriving design resistance from tests. New deck profiles, special connectors or non-standard welding conditions should be confirmed by push-out testing.

Studs make the steel beam and slab act as one, an advantage at normal temperature that brings a different force in fire: a heated composite beam expands against surrounding restraint and develops large axial thrust on its end connections and adjacent girders. NIST's investigation of 7 World Trade Center found that floor beams, made composite with the slab by shear studs, expanded on long spans at temperatures far below those normally considered in design and pushed a key girder off its seat at Column 79, starting progressive floor failures and column buckling; NIST recommended evaluating thermal expansion in buildings with composite floor systems and connections not designed for thermal effects.

Once the slab is cast, every stud is buried, and engineers altering the floor later can judge composite action only from records. Composite floors also differ by era: NIST describes the Twin Towers' floors as 4 in of lightweight concrete on light steel trusses whose bent web tops, the knuckles, projected about 3 in above the top chord into the slab to create composite action, rather than welded studs. Cutting large openings beside beams, removing slab or adding heavy equipment during alterations can reduce effective shear connection, so the original records must be used to recheck it.
evidence: 結構圖應在每根組合梁旁標示剪力釘數量與排列（單排、雙排、每肋支數），並註明是否為完全或部分組合；施工中若肋位與設計不符，須由結構工程師重新核算，而不是由現場自行減少。
設計說明應寫明每類組合梁採用的組合比及其使用性檢核結果；當樓板用途改變（例如由辦公改為實驗室或健身房）時，須以原組合比重新檢核振動與撓度。
施工圖應指定剪力釘在肋中的位置（例如一律焊在強位置），並在壓型鋼板配置圖上標示；若壓型鋼板中間有加勁肋使剪力釘無法置中，須由設計者指定偏移方向。
鋼承板配置圖應與剪力釘配置圖一起審查，確認肋位、搭接與剪力釘位置相容；鋼承板鋪設完成並經檢查後才可開始焊接剪力釘，雨後須清除肋內積水並讓板面乾燥。
剪力釘焊接人員須經訓練與資格認定，焊接程序寫明各直徑在穿板與直接焊接時的設定範圍、電源容量與最大電纜長度；接地夾須直接夾在鋼梁上並靠近焊接區。
evidenceEn: Structural drawings should note stud number and arrangement (single or double row, studs per rib) beside each composite beam and say whether it is fully or partially composite; if rib positions differ from design, the structural engineer re-checks, rather than the site reducing studs on its own.

The design basis should state the composite ratio adopted for each beam type and its serviceability results; when floor use changes, for example from office to laboratory or gym, recheck vibration and deflection with the original composite ratio.

Shop drawings should fix the stud position in the rib, for example always the strong position, and show it on the deck layout; where a stiffener in the rib prevents central placement, the designer must specify the direction of offset.

Review the deck layout together with the stud layout to confirm that rib positions, laps and stud locations are compatible; welding may start only after the deck is laid and inspected, and after rain, water must be cleared from the ribs and the surface allowed to dry.

Stud welders must be trained and qualified, and the procedure must state setting ranges for each diameter when welding through deck or direct, power-source capacity and maximum cable length; the ground clamp must be fixed directly to the steel beam close to the welding area.
pitfalls: 若施工時因壓型鋼板肋位不合或趕工而少焊剪力釘，梁在使用載重下仍看似正常，但撓度與振動比設計大，極限狀態下介面滑動使強度不足；事後補焊需要打除樓板，代價極高。
若設計以平板條件計算剪力釘強度，卻使用肋高較大的壓型鋼板並把剪力釘焊在弱位置，實際強度可能只有計算值的六成多，組合梁的極限強度與延性都不足。
電源與多支焊槍共用造成電流不足，焊瘤不完整、釘端未完全熔合，剪力釘在敲擊或彎曲時從根部脫落；接地夾夾在遠端鋼承板上，電流經由鋼承板搭接處流通，產生電弧偏吹與不穩定焊接。
若澆置時程壓縮而未完成剪力釘檢查，混凝土車到場就直接澆置，缺漏或不良的剪力釘從此無法發現；之後即使樓板裂縫或撓度異常，也很難判斷是否源自剪力釘。
若接頭只依重力剪力設計，未考慮熱膨脹產生的軸向力與位移，火災時樓板梁推動大梁或剪斷接頭螺栓，樓板失去支承後層層掉落，最後連帶柱的側向支撐失效。
pitfallsEn: If studs are omitted because rib positions do not match or work is rushed, the beam looks normal in service but deflects and vibrates more than designed, and at ultimate load interface slip leaves it short of strength; adding studs afterwards means breaking out the slab at great cost.

Designing stud strength for a solid slab, then using a deep-rib deck with studs welded in the weak position, can leave actual strength at little more than sixty percent of the calculated value, short of both ultimate strength and ductility.

A power source shared among several guns leaves current too low, giving incomplete flash and unfused stud bases that break off when tapped or bent; a ground clamp on distant decking routes current through deck laps, causing arc blow and erratic welds.

If the casting schedule is squeezed and stud inspection is incomplete when the trucks arrive, missing or defective studs are buried for good; later slab cracking or excess deflection can then hardly be traced to the studs.

If connections are designed only for gravity shear, without thermal axial force and movement, fire-heated floor beams push girders or shear connection bolts, unsupported floors fall one onto another, and columns lose their lateral bracing.

procedure: 把關鍵數據與本課算例逐項對照，標出哪些是公開工程數據、哪些是教學假設。
沿著工程時間軸，標出設計、施工、事件與維護改造的關鍵決策點，說明每個決策改變了哪一條傳力路徑或檢核。

procedureEn: Compare the key figures with this course's worked example and mark which are public project data and which are teaching assumptions.
Along the timeline, mark the key design, construction, event and retrofit decisions and say which load path or check each one changed.
Against the listed codes and standards, find the kind of clause behind this course's tests or acceptance steps, noting edition and jurisdiction.
Pick one landmark project to compare with this course and list differences in span or height, structural system, main loads and construction method.

Applying another country's clauses without checking edition, jurisdiction and load combinations.

guides.title: 傳力、算例與驗證：鋼筋混凝土剪力牆施工
guides.titleEn: Load paths, calculations and verification: Reinforced-concrete shear-wall construction
guides.concept: 剪力牆是高層與中高層建築最主要的側力抵抗構件，其耐震表現取決於牆端邊界構材的圍束、縱筋續接位置、施工縫處理與混凝土在密集鋼筋中的密實度。本課以哈里發塔的扶壁式核心牆、亞特蘭大電梯試驗塔的滑模核心牆，以及 2011 年基督城 CTV 大樓倒塌後皇家調查委員會的檢討為背景，說明側力分配、邊界構材需求、圍束配筋、續接、鋼筋間距與骨材、澆置振搗、強度驗收、澆置前查驗、震後損傷判讀與開孔變更管控。
guides.conceptEn: Shear walls are the main lateral-force-resisting members of mid- and high-rise buildings, and their seismic performance depends on confinement of boundary elements, the location of longitudinal splices, treatment of construction joints and the compaction of concrete within dense reinforcement. Against the background of Burj Khalifa's buttressed core walls, the slipformed core walls of the Atlanta elevator test tower and the Royal Commission's review after the 2011 collapse of the CTV Building in Christchurch, the course covers lateral force sharing, boundary-element demand, confinement detailing, splices, bar spacing and aggregate size, placing and vibration, strength acceptance, pre-pour inspection, post-earthquake damage interpretation and control of later openings.
procedure: 樓板像一片水平深梁，把每層的風力或地震慣性力收集起來，再依各牆的相對勁度分配給剪力牆；剪力牆以懸臂方式把剪力與彎矩傳到基礎。牆的勁度與長度三次方成正比，所以長牆分擔絕大多數側力，短牆幾乎只是跟著變形。哈里發塔由三翼各自的高性能混凝土核心牆與中央六角形核心互相扶壁，使整體抗扭勁度很高；這種「牆接牆」的佈置讓側力能在三翼之間互相分擔。施工時任何改變牆長、開口位置或樓板與牆連接的變更，都會改變這條傳力路徑。

剪力牆在地震中以牆底塑性鉸的撓曲變形消散能量，牆端受壓區的混凝土應變最高。若受壓區深度大、側向變位大，牆端混凝土會壓碎、縱筋挫屈，因此規範要求在需要時設置特殊邊界構材，以密集箍筋圍束牆端。ACI 318-19 以位移為基礎判斷是否需要邊界構材：中性軸深度 c 超過某個與牆長及設計位移相關的門檻時就需設置，並規定其水平延伸範圍。軸壓越高，c 越大，邊界構材越長，這也是為什麼高層下部牆體的端部鋼筋最密。
圍束的作用是讓被箍住的核心混凝土在高壓應變下仍能承載，並防止縱筋挫屈。圍束效果取決於箍筋面積、間距、形狀與彎鉤：箍筋需以 135° 彎鉤錨入核心，繫筋要勾住縱筋，並且間距要夠小，使每一根或每隔一根縱筋都受到側向支撐。現場最常見的問題不是鋼筋量不足，而是彎鉤角度不對、繫筋未勾住縱筋，或為了方便澆置而把箍筋間距放寬。這些錯誤在圖面上看不出來，只有在現場查驗才能發現。
剪力牆的縱筋必須逐層接續，最常見的是搭接，但搭接需要很長的長度，並使接頭處鋼筋數量加倍。塑性鉸區是地震中鋼筋反覆降伏的位置，搭接在此區容易因保護層剝落而失效，因此規範對塑性鉸區的續接位置與型式有額外限制，常改用可發展鋼筋實際強度的機械式續接器，或把搭接錯開到塑性鉸區以外。續接位置也影響施工：每層澆置高度、模板與鋼筋吊裝順序都需配合續接設計。
剪力牆邊界構材中，縱筋、箍筋、繫筋、續接與預埋件集中在很小的斷面內，混凝土必須能從鋼筋間隙流過並包覆每一根鋼筋。若鋼筋淨間距小於粗骨材能通過的寬度，骨材會在鋼筋上架橋，下方形成蜂窩與空洞，正好出現在最需要混凝土的牆端。因此設計與施工必須一起決定鋼筋配置、骨材最大粒徑、是否使用自充填混凝土，以及澆置管或振動棒能否插入。這是設計圖上的鋼筋與現場可施工性之間最常發生衝突的地方。
剪力牆又高又薄，混凝土從頂部落下時容易析離，粗骨材先落到底部堆積，砂漿留在上方；因此牆體澆置要以澆置管或軟管伸入模板內，控制自由落差，並分層澆置、逐層振搗。振動棒必須插入下層約 100 mm 使兩層結合，插入間距要小於作用半徑的 1.5 倍，並在牆端邊界構材、開口下方與施工縫等容易缺漿的位置加強振搗。亞特蘭大試驗塔的外牆厚約 460 mm、內牆約 250 mm，薄牆中振動棒的操作空間更小。
剪力牆的混凝土強度直接影響邊界構材需求、剪力強度與鋼筋握裹，因此驗收不能只看平均值。ACI 318 的驗收規則同時要求連續三組試驗的平均值達到規定強度，以及單組不得低於某個下限，前者控制整體品質，後者抓出個別不良批次。若試體結果不合格，要先檢討取樣與試驗程序，再以鑽心試驗評估結構中的實際強度；回彈錘或超音波等非破壞檢測可用來找出可疑區域與決定鑽心位置，但不能取代鑽心。
剪力牆合模之後鋼筋就看不到了，所以澆置前查驗是確認設計意圖的最後機會。查驗清單包括：鋼筋號數、數量與間距、邊界構材範圍與箍筋、彎鉤、續接位置與長度、樓板拉桿與集力構件、預埋件與開口補強、保護層墊塊與鋼筋固定、施工縫清潔。保護層不足會讓鋼筋提早鏽蝕並降低耐火性；保護層過大則減少有效深度與圍束效果。查驗應以檢查表逐項進行，並保留照片與簽名紀錄。
地震後剪力牆的損傷可從裂縫型態判讀：水平裂縫集中在牆底表示撓曲作用，斜裂縫表示剪力作用，牆端保護層剝落、縱筋外露或挫屈表示邊界構材已達高應變，牆端壓碎則是嚴重損傷。殘留裂縫寬度可以粗略推估鋼筋是否已降伏：若裂縫在地震後仍明顯張開，表示鋼筋可能已產生塑性變形。修復策略從環氧樹脂灌注、局部置換混凝土，到以鋼板、纖維複合材料或增設牆體補強，需依損傷程度與殘餘能力決定，而不是只看外觀。
剪力牆在使用期間最常遭遇的破壞來源不是地震，而是後來的開孔：機電管線、門洞、窗口或裝修改造。在剪力牆上鑽孔或切割，會減少剪力斷面、切斷縱筋或水平筋，甚至把一道長牆變成兩道短牆，改變整棟建築的側力分配。因此交接文件必須清楚標示哪些牆是剪力牆、邊界構材與塑性鉸區的位置，以及哪些範圍禁止開孔；任何開孔都要經結構工程師評估。施工期間的開孔變更也應同樣受控。
procedureEn: Floors act as horizontal deep beams that collect each storey's wind or seismic inertia force and distribute it to the shear walls in proportion to their stiffness; the walls then carry shear and moment as cantilevers to the foundation. Wall stiffness varies with the cube of length, so long walls take most of the lateral force while short walls largely follow along. At Burj Khalifa each of the three wings has its own high-performance concrete core walls, and these buttress one another through a central hexagonal core, giving very high torsional stiffness; this wall-to-wall arrangement lets lateral force be shared among the wings. During construction, any change to wall length, opening position or the floor-to-wall connection alters this load path.

In an earthquake a shear wall dissipates energy through flexural deformation at a plastic hinge near its base, and the compression zone at the wall end sees the highest concrete strain. With a deep compression zone and large drift, the wall-end concrete crushes and longitudinal bars buckle, so codes require special boundary elements, wall ends confined by closely spaced hoops, where needed. ACI 318-19 uses a displacement-based check: a boundary element is needed when the neutral-axis depth c exceeds a threshold related to wall length and design displacement, and its horizontal extent is specified. Higher axial load increases c and lengthens the boundary element, which is why wall ends in the lower storeys of tall buildings carry the densest steel.

Confinement lets the confined core carry load at high compressive strain and stops longitudinal bars from buckling. Its effectiveness depends on hoop area, spacing, shape and hooks: hoops must anchor into the core with 135° hooks, crossties must engage longitudinal bars, and spacing must be close enough that every bar or every other bar is laterally supported. The commonest site problems are not too little steel but wrong hook angles, crossties that miss the bars, or hoop spacing opened up to ease concreting. These errors are invisible on drawings and are found only by site inspection.

Wall longitudinal bars must be continued storey by storey, most often by lap splices, but laps need considerable length and double the number of bars at the splice. The plastic-hinge zone is where bars yield repeatedly in an earthquake, and laps there can fail once the cover spalls, so codes impose extra limits on splice location and type in that zone, often using mechanical couplers able to develop the bar's actual strength, or staggering laps outside the hinge region. Splice location also drives construction: lift heights, formwork and rebar lifting sequences must all suit the splice design.

In a shear-wall boundary element, longitudinal bars, hoops, crossties, splices and embeds are packed into a small section, and concrete must flow through the gaps and surround every bar. If clear spacing is less than coarse aggregate can pass, the aggregate bridges across the bars and leaves honeycombing and voids underneath, exactly at the wall ends that most need concrete. Design and construction must therefore settle together the bar layout, maximum aggregate size, whether to use self-consolidating concrete, and whether a tremie or vibrator can be inserted. This is where drawings and site buildability most often collide.

Shear walls are tall and thin, and concrete dropped from the top segregates easily, with coarse aggregate piling at the bottom and mortar staying above; walls are therefore placed through a tremie or hose lowered into the form to limit free fall, in layers vibrated one by one. The vibrator must penetrate about 100 mm into the layer below to knit the layers together, with insertion spacing less than 1.5 times its radius of action, and extra attention at boundary elements, under openings and at construction joints where paste is easily lacking. The Atlanta test tower's exterior walls were about 460 mm thick and its interior walls about 250 mm, leaving even less room to work a vibrator in the thinner walls.

Shear-wall concrete strength directly affects boundary-element demand, shear strength and bond, so acceptance cannot rest on the average alone. ACI 318 acceptance requires both that every three consecutive tests average at least the specified strength and that no single test falls below a lower bound; the first controls overall quality and the second catches individual bad batches. If specimens fail, first review sampling and testing, then assess in-place strength by coring; rebound hammer or ultrasonic tests help locate suspect zones and choose core locations but cannot replace cores.

Once wall forms close, the reinforcement disappears, so the pre-pour inspection is the last chance to confirm the design intent. The checklist covers bar sizes, numbers and spacing, boundary-element extent and hoops, hooks, splice locations and lengths, floor drag bars and collectors, embeds and reinforcement around openings, cover spacers and bar fixing, and cleanliness of construction joints. Too little cover lets bars corrode early and reduces fire resistance; too much reduces effective depth and confinement. Inspection should follow the checklist item by item with photographs and signatures kept on record.

After an earthquake, shear-wall damage can be read from crack patterns: horizontal cracks concentrated at the base indicate flexure, diagonal cracks indicate shear, spalled cover with exposed or buckled bars at wall ends shows the boundary element reached high strain, and crushing at the wall end is severe damage. Residual crack width gives a rough indication of whether bars have yielded: cracks that stay clearly open after shaking suggest plastic deformation in the steel. Repair ranges from epoxy injection and local concrete replacement to strengthening with steel plates, fibre composites or added walls, chosen by damage level and residual capacity rather than appearance alone.

The commonest threat to shear walls in service is not earthquakes but later openings: services penetrations, doors, windows or fit-out changes. Drilling or cutting a shear wall reduces shear area, cuts vertical or horizontal bars and may turn one long wall into two short ones, changing the lateral force distribution of the whole building. Handover documents must therefore clearly identify which walls are shear walls, where boundary elements and plastic-hinge zones are, and which areas must not be penetrated, with every opening assessed by a structural engineer. Opening changes during construction need the same control.
evidence: 施工圖必須明示樓板與剪力牆之間的集力構件、拉桿與錨定長度，並列為澆置前查驗項目；任何牆體開口或牆長變更，須經結構設計者重新分析並書面同意。
施工圖應以獨立的牆端詳圖標示邊界構材範圍、箍筋與繫筋間距及延伸高度，現場以噴漆在模板與鋼筋上標記範圍；邊界構材查驗列為停檢點，由監造逐道簽認。
鋼筋加工圖要明示所有邊界構材箍筋與繫筋的彎鉤角度與延伸長度，加工廠出貨前抽檢；現場不得以「方便施工」為由調整箍筋間距或彎鉤，任何調整都須設計者書面同意。
結構圖應標示塑性鉸區範圍以及該區允許的續接型式；續接器供應商的認證、現場抽樣試驗與鎖緊檢查紀錄要納入品質文件，未經驗收的批次不得使用。
在施工圖階段召開鋼筋可施工性檢討，由設計者、鋼筋承包商與混凝土供應商共同決定搭接錯開、續接器使用與骨材粒徑；最擁擠的節點應先做足尺樣板並列為停檢點。
evidenceEn: Shop drawings must show collectors, drag bars and anchorage lengths between floors and shear walls and include them in pre-pour inspection; any change in wall openings or length needs re-analysis and written approval by the structural designer.

Shop drawings should give separate wall-end details showing boundary-element extent, hoop and crosstie spacing and height, with the zones spray-marked on forms and steel on site; boundary-element inspection is a hold point signed wall by wall by the resident engineer.

Bar-bending schedules must state hook angles and extensions for every boundary hoop and crosstie, with sampling at the fabrication shop before delivery; site crews may not change hoop spacing or hooks for convenience, and any change needs the designer's written approval.

Structural drawings should mark the plastic-hinge zone and the splice types allowed in it; supplier certification, site sample tests and tightening records for couplers belong in the quality file, and unaccepted batches may not be used.

Hold a rebar buildability review at shop-drawing stage where designer, rebar contractor and concrete supplier jointly decide lap staggering, coupler use and aggregate size; mock up the most congested joints at full size first and make them a hold point.
pitfalls: 樓板與牆之間的連接（集力構件、拉桿）不足時，地震中樓板無法把慣性力交給剪力牆，牆體雖然完好，樓板卻從牆上脫開；皇家調查委員會對基督城 CTV 大樓的報告即專章檢討其結構系統與樓板拉桿補強。
箍筋以 90° 彎鉤收尾，地震中保護層剝落後彎鉤張開，箍筋失去圍束，牆端混凝土壓碎、縱筋挫屈；繫筋只勾住箍筋而未勾住縱筋，縱筋在反覆載重下向外鼓出。
鋼筋過密導致粗骨材卡在箍筋上方，拆模後牆端出現大面積蜂窩，需鑿除重澆；為了讓混凝土流過而現場加水，強度下降並增加收縮裂縫。
試體在工地曝曬或搬運不當而強度偏低，誤判結構不合格；反之，只看平均值而忽略某一批次明顯偏低，該批次正好用在底層剪力牆的邊界構材，日後在地震中成為最弱處。
只以環氧樹脂灌注把裂縫填滿就宣告修復，卻未檢查已挫屈或疲勞的縱筋，下一次地震時牆端在原位置迅速破壞；修補時鑿除混凝土過深，切斷或損傷原有箍筋，反而降低圍束。
pitfallsEn: If the connections between floors and walls, collectors and drag bars, are inadequate, floors cannot deliver inertia forces to the shear walls in an earthquake, and floors may separate from walls that remain intact; the Royal Commission's report on Christchurch's CTV Building devotes sections to its structural system and the drag-bar retrofit.

Hoops finished with 90° hooks open up once the cover spalls in an earthquake, losing confinement so the wall-end concrete crushes and bars buckle; crossties hooked only around hoops and not around longitudinal bars let those bars bow outward under cyclic load.

Excessive congestion traps coarse aggregate above hoops and leaves extensive honeycombing at wall ends after stripping, requiring break-out and recasting; adding water on site to make concrete flow cuts strength and increases shrinkage cracking.

Specimens left in the sun or mishandled read low and wrongly condemn the structure; conversely, watching only the average while ignoring one clearly low batch, used precisely in a ground-storey boundary element, leaves the weakest point where earthquakes hit hardest.

Declaring a wall repaired after merely filling cracks with epoxy, without checking for buckled or fatigued longitudinal bars, lets the wall end fail quickly at the same spot in the next earthquake; breaking out too deep during repair cuts or damages existing hoops and reduces confinement.
