guides.title: 傳力、算例與驗證：預鑄混凝土耐震接頭
guides.titleEn: Load paths, calculations and verification: Seismic connections for precast concrete
guides.concept: 從預鑄構架的地震傳力路徑與自復位原理出發，計算混合預力梁柱接頭的開口、鋼腱應力與軟鋼脫黏長度，設計灌漿套筒續接，再處理吊裝期間的臨時穩定、樓梯與樓板的支承長度與滑動縫、ACI 374.1 試驗允收與 PRESSS 縮尺試驗，最後談套筒灌漿缺陷檢測與震後預力復驗，並以 The Paramount、PRESSS 試驗建築與基督城地震的公開教訓對照。
guides.conceptEn: Starting from the seismic load path of precast frames and the principle of self-centring, compute gap opening, tendon stress and mild-steel debonded length in hybrid post-tensioned beam–column joints and design grouted sleeve splices, then handle temporary stability during erection, seating length and sliding joints for stairs and floors, ACI 374.1 test acceptance and the PRESSS scaled test, and finally detection of sleeve grouting defects and post-earthquake prestress checks, compared with public lessons from The Paramount, the PRESSS test building and the Christchurch earthquake.
procedure: 現澆混凝土建築的連續性是自然形成的，預鑄建築則必須由接頭刻意建立：樓板慣性力經板間接合器、弦材與集力構件傳到抗側力牆或構架，再經柱底或牆底接頭進入基礎。任何一段接頭不足，整條路徑就斷開。設計上有兩種策略：等同現澆（emulative）讓接頭比構件更強，把塑性鉸推離接頭；接合式（jointed）則讓變形集中在接頭本身，以預力與耗能元件控制行為。1994 年 Northridge 地震中預鑄停車結構的倒塌，正是傳力路徑在接頭處中斷的典型。
接合式預鑄構架把梁與柱以無黏結預力鋼腱夾在一起，地震時梁端與柱面之間張開一個縫，構件本身幾乎不受損；預力在震後把縫重新壓合，使結構回到原位，這就是自復位。只有預力時遲滯迴圈幾乎沒有面積，耗能不足，因此再加入會降伏的軟鋼筋或耗能元件，得到形如旗子的遲滯迴圈：既能耗能，又能在卸載後歸零。關鍵在於預力提供的回復彎矩必須大於軟鋼的降伏彎矩，否則殘留變位無法消除。
混合接頭（hybrid connection）由穿過柱的無黏結預力鋼腱與梁上下緣灌漿套管內的軟鋼筋組成。層間變位幾乎全部轉為梁端開口轉角，開口在鋼腱處造成伸長，因鋼腱無黏結，伸長分攤到整段長度，應力增加有限、保持彈性；軟鋼筋則在接頭附近刻意脫黏一段長度，讓伸長分散在這段長度內，控制應變以避免低週疲勞斷裂。The Paramount 等預鑄混合構架建築即採用此類接頭概念。
等同現澆的預鑄柱常以灌漿套筒把柱主筋與基礎或下層柱的鋼筋續接：下方鋼筋插入預埋在柱底的鋼套筒，再以高強無收縮灌漿填滿，鋼筋力經灌漿黏結與套筒內的凸肋傳遞。柱底正是塑性鉸區，續接器必須能發展鋼筋的抗拉強度而不先破壞，才能讓塑性變形留在鋼筋上。接頭的弱點在施工：插筋錯位、套筒灌漿不滿或灌漿強度不足，外觀完全看不出來。
預鑄構件在接頭灌漿、焊接或預力完成之前，只是彼此擱置的獨立構件，抗側力與穩定都依賴臨時斜撐、墊塊與臨時螺栓。施工階段的風、吊車碰撞或小地震，都可能在此時造成連續傾倒。因此吊裝計畫必須定義每一階段的穩定系統：哪些構件先完成永久接頭、臨時斜撐何時可以拆除、上方可以吊裝多少層而不超過下方未灌漿接頭的能力。

預鑄樓梯與樓板擱置在梁或牛腿上，地震時上下樓層產生相對位移，若樓梯兩端都被固定，它會像斜撐一樣受壓而破壞；若一端設計為滑動，滑動量與支承長度必須足以容納最大層間變位，並保留施工誤差與邊緣剝落的餘裕。2011 年基督城地震中，Forsyth Barr 大樓與 Grand Chancellor 飯店的預鑄樓梯崩落，就是滑動縫與支承長度不足以容納層間變位的教訓，紐西蘭皇家調查委員會報告對建築非主結構構件的變位相容提出檢討。
接合式預鑄構架的行為不能完全以現澆規範推論，因此 ACI 374.1 以結構試驗作為允收依據：以實尺度或大尺度梁柱子結構承受逐級增大的反覆位移，至少到 3.5% 層間變位，並檢查強度保持、相對能量消散比與卸載後的勁度。ACI 550.3 則針對以無黏結預力形成的預鑄特殊抗彎構架，規定在符合這些試驗允收的前提下的設計方法。試驗的價值是同時證明強度、韌性與耗能，而不是只看最大承載力。

接頭試驗證明單一接頭，系統試驗則檢查整棟建築中樓板、接頭、牆與構架是否協同運作。1999 年在加州大學聖地牙哥分校完成的 PRESSS 五層預鑄試驗建築，以約 60% 縮尺在同一棟試驗建築的兩個方向分別放入多種預鑄構架與接合式剪力牆系統，以擬動態方式施加逐級增大的地震，驗證了混合構架與接合式牆的自復位與低損傷表現，後續影響了 ACI 規範與 The Paramount 等建築。縮尺試驗必須了解相似律，才能把試驗力量換回實尺度。
預鑄接頭最難管理的是隱蔽在混凝土內的部分：灌漿套筒、預力套管、預埋鋼板與焊接接合器，一旦封閉就無法目視。檢測必須在施工中留下紀錄，並在完工後以非破壞方法抽查，例如超音波、X 光或衝擊回音法檢測套筒灌漿飽滿度，內視鏡檢查預力套管，鋼筋掃描確認預埋件位置。使用期間則以防水、防蝕與定期檢查維持外露接合器與預埋鋼板的狀態。
接合式預鑄建築的優點是震後損傷少、可快速復原，但必須證明預力仍在、縫已閉合、樓梯與樓板支承未移位。震後檢查要量測殘留層間變位、梁端殘留開口、軟鋼脫黏段附近的混凝土狀態，並以千斤頂浮升試驗確認鋼腱預力；等同現澆的接頭則檢查柱底與梁端塑性鉸區裂縫與剝落。交接文件需記錄每種接頭的位置、型式、預力值與檢測紀錄，讓未來的評估有依據。
procedureEn: Continuity in cast-in-place concrete arises naturally, whereas in precast buildings it must be created deliberately by connections: floor inertia forces travel through panel-to-panel connectors, chords and collectors to lateral walls or frames, then through column-base or wall-base joints into the foundation. If any connection is inadequate, the path is broken. Design follows one of two strategies: emulative, making connections stronger than members so plastic hinges move away from the joints, or jointed, concentrating deformation in the joints themselves and controlling it with prestress and dissipating elements. Collapses of precast parking structures in the 1994 Northridge earthquake typify a load path broken at the connections.

A jointed precast frame clamps beams to columns with unbonded post-tensioning tendons; in an earthquake a gap opens between beam end and column face while the members themselves stay nearly undamaged, and after shaking the prestress closes the gap and returns the structure to its original position, which is self-centring. Prestress alone gives hysteresis loops with almost no area and too little dissipation, so yielding mild-steel bars or dissipating devices are added to produce a flag-shaped loop that both dissipates energy and returns to zero on unloading. The key is that the restoring moment from prestress must exceed the yield moment of the mild steel, otherwise residual drift cannot be removed.

A hybrid connection combines unbonded post-tensioning tendons through the column with mild-steel bars grouted in ducts at the top and bottom of the beam. Almost all storey drift becomes gap-opening rotation at the beam end, which elongates the tendon; being unbonded, the tendon spreads the elongation over its full length, so stress rises modestly and stays elastic, while the mild bars are deliberately debonded over a short length near the joint so their elongation is spread over that length, limiting strain and avoiding low-cycle fatigue fracture. Precast hybrid-frame buildings such as The Paramount use this connection concept.

Emulative precast columns often splice their main bars to foundation or lower-column bars with grouted sleeves: the lower bars enter steel sleeves cast into the column base, which are then filled with high-strength non-shrink grout, and bar force transfers through grout bond and ribs inside the sleeve. The column base is exactly the plastic-hinge zone, so the splice must develop the bar's tensile strength without failing first, keeping plastic deformation in the bars. The weakness lies in construction: misaligned dowels, partly filled sleeves or weak grout are completely invisible from outside.

Before connections are grouted, welded or post-tensioned, precast members are independent pieces resting on each other, relying on temporary braces, shims and erection bolts for lateral resistance and stability. Wind, crane impact or a small earthquake during this phase can trigger progressive toppling. The erection plan must therefore define the stability system at every stage: which members receive permanent connections first, when temporary braces may be removed, and how many levels may be erected above ungrouted joints without exceeding their capacity.

Precast stairs and floor units sit on beams or corbels; in an earthquake the floors above and below move relative to each other, and a stair fixed at both ends acts like a brace and fails in compression. If one end is designed to slide, the sliding allowance and seating length must accommodate the maximum storey drift plus margins for construction tolerance and edge spalling. In the 2011 Christchurch earthquake, precast stairs collapsed in the Forsyth Barr building and the Hotel Grand Chancellor, a lesson in sliding joints and seats too small for storey drift, and the Canterbury Earthquakes Royal Commission reviewed the deformation compatibility of elements outside the primary structure.

The behaviour of jointed precast frames cannot be inferred entirely from cast-in-place rules, so ACI 374.1 makes structural testing the basis for acceptance: full- or large-scale beam–column subassemblies are cycled at increasing displacements up to at least 3.5% drift, and strength retention, relative energy-dissipation ratio and stiffness around zero are checked. ACI 550.3 then gives design methods for precast special moment frames with unbonded post-tensioning that satisfy these acceptance criteria. The value of testing is that it proves strength, ductility and dissipation together rather than peak capacity alone.

Joint tests prove single connections; system tests check that floors, joints, walls and frames work together in a whole building. The PRESSS five-storey precast test building, completed at the University of California, San Diego in 1999 at about 60% scale, placed several precast frame types in one direction and a jointed shear-wall system in the other, applied earthquakes of increasing intensity pseudodynamically, and demonstrated the self-centring, low-damage behaviour of hybrid frames and jointed walls, later influencing ACI provisions and buildings such as The Paramount. Scaled tests require an understanding of similitude to convert test forces back to full scale.

The hardest part of precast connections to manage is what lies hidden inside concrete: grouted sleeves, post-tensioning ducts, embedded plates and welded connectors cannot be seen once closed. Inspection must leave records during construction and be followed by non-destructive sampling after completion, for example ultrasonic, X-ray or impact-echo checks of sleeve grout fill, borescopes in post-tensioning ducts and cover scanning to locate embeds. In service, waterproofing, corrosion protection and periodic inspection maintain exposed connectors and embedded plates.

The advantage of jointed precast buildings is little damage and quick recovery after an earthquake, but engineers must prove that prestress remains, gaps have closed and stair and floor seats have not shifted. Post-earthquake inspection measures residual drift and residual gap at beam ends, examines concrete near the debonded mild-steel zones and confirms tendon force by jack lift-off tests; emulative joints are checked for cracking and spalling in column-base and beam-end hinge zones. Handover records must document every connection's location, type, prestress and inspection results to support future assessments.
evidence: 設計說明應明列整棟建築採用的耐震策略與每種接頭的類別，並要求預鑄廠的接頭細部圖由結構技師核可；未經核可不得以其他接頭替代。
設計者應同時設定耗能與復位兩個目標，並在圖說中標明預力值、軟鋼面積與允許偏差；任何現場變更預力束數或鋼筋量，都須重新計算 λ 並經核可。
圖說要以明顯符號標示「無黏結鋼腱」與「軟鋼脫黏段」，灌漿作業前由監造確認脫黏套管封堵完整，並設為停止點；錨碇與鋼腱的防蝕細節須可檢查。
柱吊裝就位前以樣板確認插筋位置，偏差超過允許值須由設計者決定處置，嚴禁現場熱彎；灌漿作業由受訓人員執行，逐支記錄出漿確認與灌漿批號，並設為柱上方構件安裝前的停止點。
吊裝計畫須由具資格的工程師簽認，列明每一階段的穩定系統、斜撐拆除條件與停工風速；這是工程檢核的停止點，不是吊掛作業的操作許可。
evidenceEn: The design basis should state the seismic strategy for the building and the category of every connection type, with the precaster's connection details approved by the structural engineer; no substitution without approval.

Designers should set both dissipation and recentring targets and show prestress, mild-steel area and tolerances on drawings; any site change in strand count or bar area requires recalculating λ and approval.

Drawings should mark ‘unbonded tendon’ and ‘mild-steel debonded zone’ prominently, and before grouting the site supervisor must confirm that debonding sleeves are sealed, as a hold point; anchorage and tendon corrosion protection must be inspectable.

Check dowel positions with a template before setting each column; deviations beyond tolerance go to the designer, and hot bending on site is forbidden; grouting is done by trained operatives, with outlet flow and grout batch logged for every sleeve as a hold point before members above are erected.

The erection plan must be signed by a qualified engineer, stating the stability system at every stage, brace-removal conditions and stop-work wind speeds; it is an engineering hold point, not an operating permit for rigging.
pitfalls: 隔板接合器或集力構件不足時，地震中樓板與牆分離，樓板失去側向支撐，柱承受未設計的大變形而破壞；若只依重力荷載設計擱置支承，板件在大變位下從支承滑落。
若脫黏長度在現場被灌漿填滿或過短，軟鋼應變集中在數公分內，在幾個大循環後斷裂，接頭失去耗能；鋼腱若因錨碇處腐蝕或灌漿誤入而變成部分黏結，大變位時局部降伏，預力永久損失，自復位能力下降。
為了加快進度而在接頭灌漿強度未達前拆除斜撐，強風時牆板或柱傾倒並撞倒相鄰構件；墊塊材料或位置錯誤使構件偏心擱置，灌漿後殘留應力，日後在接頭處開裂。
若以試體縮尺過小或細部簡化的試驗結果套用到實際接頭，混凝土保護層剝落、灌漿與錨碇行為都不相同，實際接頭可能在較小變位就失去強度；只看最大力而忽略第三循環的強度衰減，會高估韌性。
若只依賴施工人員的口頭確認而沒有紀錄與抽查，灌漿缺陷可能大量存在而無人知曉，直到地震時多根柱同時在柱底拔出；外露的焊接接合器在停車場等潮濕環境中鏽蝕，斷面減少使隔板傳力能力下降。
pitfallsEn: With inadequate diaphragm connectors or collectors, floors separate from walls in an earthquake, columns lose lateral support and fail under undesigned deformation; bearings designed for gravity alone let units slide off at large displacement.

If the debonded length is filled with grout on site or made too short, mild-steel strain concentrates over a few centimetres and the bar fractures after a few large cycles, losing dissipation; tendons made partly bonded by anchorage corrosion or stray grout yield locally at large drift, permanently losing prestress and recentring ability.

Removing braces before joint grout gains strength to save time lets panels or columns topple in strong wind and knock down neighbours; wrong shim material or position leaves members eccentrically seated, locking in stresses that later crack the joint.

Applying results from a specimen that is too small or simplified to real joints ignores differences in cover spalling, grouting and anchorage, so real joints may lose strength at smaller drifts; looking only at peak force and ignoring third-cycle strength decay overstates ductility.

Relying on verbal assurances without records or sampling can leave widespread grouting defects unknown until an earthquake pulls out many column bases at once; exposed welded connectors in damp environments such as car parks corrode, losing section and diaphragm capacity.

guides.scope: 依公開工程原理、官方資料與規範架構編寫的原創教學；步驟是可驗證的學習任務與假想算例，不是設計圖說、施工計畫、吊裝或張拉作業許可，也不是任何專案的設計文件。數值均為教學假設或公開資料，實際工程須由合格技師依規範與實測資料重新計算並簽證。
guides.scopeEn: Original teaching built from public engineering principles, official sources and code frameworks. Steps are verifiable learning tasks and hypothetical exercises, not design drawings, method statements, lifting or stressing permits, or any project's design documents. Numbers are teaching assumptions or public data; real work must be recalculated and certified by qualified engineers using codes and measured data.

guides.conceptEn: Section properties, prestress camber, dapped ends, flange connectors and completed erection connections that keep double-tee roofs reliable from plant to service. Figures come from public sources and are rounded for learning comparisons; they are not design values.
facts: Montgomery Mall 事故中的雙 T 梁長約 60 ft（約 18.3 m）、寬 9 ft、深 2 ft 3 in，重約 42,800 lb（約 19.4 t）
Montgomery Mall 雙 T 梁翼板最小厚 4 in，兩腹肋間距 4 ft 6 in
2012 年邁阿密戴德學院停車場為 6 層、305 ft × 390 ft，倒塌範圍約 122 ft × 132 ft，4 人罹難
該次倒塌的混凝土約 3,300 tons，其中雙 T 梁約 3,000 tons
職業安全衛生署估計未灌漿柱底承受約 1,360 kips，超過 839 至 1,050 kips 的估計承壓能力
該停車場雙 T 梁深 30 in、寬 12 ft、翼板 4 in，契約要求柱底在吊裝後 48 小時內灌漿
2016 年重建停車場當天放置 7 片雙 T 梁，其中 4 片只有 1 處或沒有完成規定的 4 處端部焊接
PCI 設計手冊目前為第 9 版
factsEn: The Montgomery Mall double tee was about 60 ft (about 18.3 m) long, 9 ft wide and 2 ft 3 in deep, weighing about 42,800 lb (about 19.4 t)
The Montgomery Mall double tee had a 4 in minimum flange and stems 4 ft 6 in apart
The 2012 Miami Dade College garage was 6 storeys and 305 ft × 390 ft; the collapse covered about 122 ft × 132 ft and killed 4 workers
About 3,300 tons of concrete fell in that collapse, including about 3,000 tons of double tees
OSHA estimated about 1,360 kips on the ungrouted column base, above an estimated bearing capacity of 839 to 1,050 kips
That garage used double tees 30 in deep and 12 ft wide with 4 in flanges, and the contract required column-base grout within 48 hours of erection
At the rebuilt garage in 2016, 7 double tees were placed that day and 4 had 1 or none of the 4 required end welds
The PCI Design Handbook is currently in its 9th edition

timelineEn: 1954 — The Precast/Prestressed Concrete Institute (PCI) is founded to advance design and manufacturing standards for prestressed members
1990 — Precast roof members collapse during placement at the Greater Pittsburgh International Airport airside building
2012 — The Miami Dade College garage under construction collapses from an ungrouted column base, with double tees falling in cascade
2013 — A temporary support buckles and collapses while a double tee is removed by jacking at Montgomery Mall
2016 — Two double tees collapse at the rebuilt Miami Dade College garage with end welds incomplete

procedure: 把關鍵數據與本課算例逐項對照，標出哪些是公開工程數據、哪些是教學假設。
沿著工程時間軸，標出設計、施工、事件與維護改造的關鍵決策點，說明每個決策改變了哪一條傳力路徑或檢核。
對照列出的規範與標準，找出本課試驗或允收步驟對應的條款類型，並註明版本與適用地區。
從代表工程中選一個與本課比較，列出跨度或高度、結構系統、主要荷載與施工方法的差異。
procedureEn: Compare the key figures with this course's worked example and mark which are public project data and which are teaching assumptions.
Along the timeline, mark the key design, construction, event and retrofit decisions and say which load path or check each one changed.
Against the listed codes and standards, find the kind of clause behind this course's tests or acceptance steps, noting edition and jurisdiction.
Pick one landmark project to compare with this course and list differences in span or height, structural system, main loads and construction method.
pitfalls: 把四捨五入的公開數據當成設計值或允收值使用。

pitfallsEn: Using rounded public figures as design or acceptance values.
Applying another country's clauses without checking edition, jurisdiction and load combinations.

Numbers are teaching assumptions or public data; real work must be recalculated and certified by qualified engineers using codes and measured data.

guides.title: 傳力、算例與驗證：預鑄預力雙 T 梁屋蓋
guides.titleEn: Load paths, calculations and verification: Precast prestressed double-tee roofs
guides.concept: 從雙 T 梁斷面與屋頂荷載路徑出發，計算預力反拱與長期撓度、缺口梁端吊筋與水平束制力、翼板連接器的隔板剪力，再處理吊裝期間的臨時穩定與連接完成、反拱差與屋面排水、放鬆時端部應力與出廠品質、現場載重試驗，最後談屋面防水與連接器腐蝕、改裝開孔與交接，並以美國職業安全衛生署對邁阿密戴德學院停車場與 Montgomery Mall 雙 T 梁事故的調查報告對照。
guides.conceptEn: Starting from the double-tee section and the roof load path, compute prestress camber and long-term deflection, dapped-end hangers and horizontal restraint forces, and diaphragm shear on flange connectors, then handle temporary stability and completed connections during erection, camber differential and roof drainage, end stresses at transfer and plant quality, and in-situ load testing, and finally roof waterproofing and connector corrosion, alterations and handover, compared with OSHA investigation reports on the Miami Dade College garage and Montgomery Mall double-tee incidents.
procedure: 雙 T 梁由一片薄翼板與兩根腹肋組成：翼板同時是屋面板與受壓區，兩根腹肋內配置預力鋼絞線，像兩根並排的 T 形梁一樣跨越 15 至 30 m 左右的跨度。屋頂荷載包括自重、防水與設備的附加靜載、活載或雪載與積水雨載，經翼板傳到腹肋，再經腹肋端部擱置在倒 T 梁、牆或牛腿上的承壓墊。翼板之間以焊接連接器相連，使整片屋頂成為傳遞風與地震力的隔板。這個系統輕、快、跨度大，但每一個端部與連接器都是關鍵。
預力鋼絞線偏心配置在腹肋下方，放鬆後產生向上的彎矩，使雙 T 梁向上拱起，這就是反拱；自重則產生向下撓度。之後混凝土潛變使反拱隨時間增長，但預力損失與附加靜載又會抵銷一部分。對屋頂而言，反拱關係到排水坡度、防水層、與相鄰構件的高差，以及屋面設備與天窗的安裝。PCI 設計手冊提供以乘數估算安裝時與長期撓度的簡化方法。
為了讓屋頂高程平順，雙 T 梁腹肋端部常做成缺口（dapped end），擱置在倒 T 梁或牆的承壓墊上。缺口的內角是應力集中處，剪力必須靠吊筋把力從下方的缺口段傳到上方全斷面，並配置水平鋼筋抵抗端部水平力。承壓墊讓構件因乾縮、潛變與溫度變化而自由伸縮；若端部被焊死或承壓墊被灌漿填滿，這些體積變化會被束制，產生水平拉力，使缺口內角開裂。
沒有現澆面層的雙 T 梁屋頂，隔板作用完全依賴相鄰翼板之間的焊接連接器與周邊弦材：連接器傳遞翼板接縫上的剪力，同時讓相鄰構件的撓度協調，避免集中荷載只由一片雙 T 梁承受。弦材與集力構件把隔板力送到抗側力牆或構架。連接器間距、預埋鋼件的錨定與現場焊接品質，決定了屋頂能否在風與地震中作為一個整體。

雙 T 梁吊裝快速，但在端部與翼板連接完成前，每一片都只是擱置在承壓墊上的獨立構件，支承它的柱、倒 T 梁與牆也可能尚未灌漿或焊接完成。美國職業安全衛生署的調查顯示：2012 年邁阿密戴德學院停車場倒塌，起因是一根柱底未灌漿而由墊片承壓，柱荷載約 1,360 kips 超過估計承壓能力 839 至 1,050 kips；2016 年重建工地則有兩片雙 T 梁在相鄰構件調整墊片時倒塌，當天放置的 7 片中有 4 片只有一處或沒有完成規定的 4 處端部焊接。
相鄰雙 T 梁因混凝土強度、放鬆時間與堆置天數不同，反拱可能相差十幾公釐，翼板接縫出現高低差。焊接連接器前必須先把高差拉平，通常以夾具、千斤頂或加載方式調整，強行焊接則會在連接器與翼板中留下應力。另一方面，雙 T 梁屋頂的長期淨反拱往往很小，屋面排水坡度若不足，暴雨時積水增加荷載，形成積水—撓度—更多積水的循環，因此屋頂的雨水荷載與排水設計和結構設計密不可分。
預力放鬆是雙 T 梁最危險的時刻之一：混凝土強度還低，跨中有自重彎矩抵銷預力偏心，但梁端附近沒有自重彎矩，底部壓應力與頂部拉應力都最大。若頂部拉應力超過容許值，翼板會開裂，因此常把部分鋼絞線在端部脫黏、把鋼絞線折線配置，或在頂部配置黏結鋼筋。工廠品質管理還包括放鬆強度試體、尺寸與預埋件位置、反拱量測與端部裂縫檢查，PCI 設有工廠認證制度。
當雙 T 梁在運輸、吊裝或使用中受損，或屋頂要增加超出原設計的荷載，而計算無法確認安全時，可做現場載重試驗：以水袋或砂包分級加載，量測跨中撓度、裂縫與卸載後的回復。預力構件在未開裂時撓度接近線性且回復良好，若加載過程撓度突然增加或回復不足，代表已開裂或預力鋼絞線受損。試驗本身有風險，必須事先設計荷載級距、停止條件與安全支撐。
無面層的雙 T 梁屋頂有大量翼板接縫，接縫密封與防水層一旦失效，雨水會沿接縫滲入，直接接觸焊接連接器、預埋鋼件與承壓區。連接器多為外露鋼板，在潮濕與乾濕循環下腐蝕，斷面減少使隔板傳力能力下降；承壓區長期潮濕則使缺口端部鋼筋鏽蝕、混凝土剝落。屋面維護因此不只是防漏，而是保護結構連接。

雙 T 梁屋頂在使用期間常因增設空調、太陽能板或天窗而開孔或加載。翼板可在腹肋之間有限度開孔，但腹肋內的預力鋼絞線絕對不可切斷，切斷一股就直接減少強度並可能使端部錨定失效。移除或搬移既有雙 T 梁同樣危險：職業安全衛生署調查的 2013 年 Montgomery Mall 事故，是以千斤頂與滑移方式移除一片長約 60 ft、重約 42,800 lb 的雙 T 梁時，臨時支撐塔頂部鋼梁受壓挫屈，造成一死一傷。
procedureEn: A double tee consists of a thin flange and two stems: the flange is both roof deck and compression zone, while prestressing strands in the stems let the unit span roughly 15 to 30 m like two T-beams side by side. Roof loads, namely self-weight, superimposed dead load from roofing and equipment, live or snow load and ponding rain, pass from the flange into the stems and then through bearing pads at the stem ends onto inverted-tee beams, walls or corbels. Flanges are joined by welded connectors so that the whole roof acts as a diaphragm carrying wind and earthquake forces. The system is light, fast and long-spanning, but every end bearing and connector is critical.

Strands placed eccentrically low in the stems create an upward moment at release, bowing the tee upward, which is camber, while self-weight produces downward deflection. Creep then increases camber with time, partly offset by prestress losses and superimposed dead load. For a roof, camber affects drainage slope, waterproofing, level differences with adjacent members, and the fit of equipment and skylights. The PCI Design Handbook offers a simplified multiplier method to estimate deflections at erection and in the long term.

To keep roof levels smooth, stem ends are often dapped and seated on bearing pads on inverted-tee beams or walls. The re-entrant corner of a dap concentrates stress, so hanger reinforcement must lift shear from the reduced nib into the full section above, with horizontal bars resisting end tension. Bearing pads let the member move freely with shrinkage, creep and temperature change; if ends are welded rigidly or pads are grouted solid, these volume changes are restrained and create horizontal tension that cracks the dap corner.

In an untopped double-tee roof, diaphragm action relies entirely on welded connectors between adjacent flanges and on perimeter chords: connectors transfer shear along flange joints and make adjacent members deflect together, so a concentrated load is not carried by one tee alone. Chords and collectors deliver diaphragm force to lateral walls or frames. Connector spacing, anchorage of embedded hardware and field weld quality decide whether the roof works as one unit in wind and earthquakes.

Double tees go up quickly, but until end and flange connections are complete each unit is just a member resting on pads, and the columns, inverted tees and walls supporting it may themselves be ungrouted or unwelded. OSHA investigations show that the 2012 Miami Dade College garage collapse began at a column whose base was never grouted and bore on shims, with a column load of about 1,360 kips exceeding an estimated bearing capacity of 839 to 1,050 kips; at the rebuilt garage in 2016, two tees fell while shims were adjusted on an adjacent member, and four of the seven placed that day had one or none of the four required end welds.

Adjacent double tees can differ in camber by more than ten millimetres because of different concrete strength, release time and storage age, leaving steps at flange joints. These must be pulled level before connectors are welded, usually with clamps, jacks or surcharge, since forced welding locks stresses into connectors and flanges. Moreover, long-term net camber of a double-tee roof is often small, so with too little drainage slope a downpour ponds water, adding load in a ponding–deflection–more-ponding cycle; rain load and drainage design are therefore inseparable from the structural design of the roof.

Strand release is one of the most critical moments for a double tee: concrete strength is still low, and while self-weight moment at midspan offsets prestress eccentricity, near the ends there is no self-weight moment, so bottom compression and top tension are both greatest. If top tension exceeds its limit the flange cracks, so some strands are debonded at the ends, strands are harped, or bonded top reinforcement is added. Plant quality control also covers release-strength cylinders, dimensions and embed positions, camber measurement and end-crack inspection, and PCI runs a plant certification programme.

When a double tee has been damaged in transport, erection or service, or a roof must carry more load than designed and calculation cannot confirm safety, an in-situ load test may be used: water bags or sandbags are added in stages while midspan deflection, cracking and recovery after unloading are measured. Uncracked prestressed members deflect almost linearly and recover well; a sudden jump in deflection or poor recovery signals cracking or strand damage. Testing itself carries risk, so load increments, stop criteria and safety shoring must be designed beforehand.

An untopped double-tee roof has many flange joints, and once joint sealants and membrane fail, rain runs into the joints and onto welded connectors, embedded steel and bearing areas. Connectors are usually exposed steel plates that corrode under wetting and drying, losing section and diaphragm capacity; persistently damp bearing areas rust dap reinforcement and spall concrete. Roof maintenance is therefore not only about leaks but about protecting structural connections.

Double-tee roofs are often cut or loaded in service for new air-conditioning, solar panels or skylights. The flange may take limited openings between stems, but strands inside the stems must never be cut, since cutting even one strand directly reduces strength and may undermine end anchorage. Removing or relocating existing tees is equally hazardous: in the 2013 Montgomery Mall incident investigated by OSHA, a tee about 60 ft long weighing about 42,800 lb was being removed by jacking and skating when the top beam of a temporary safety tower buckled, killing one worker and injuring another.
evidence: 設計與機電要在初期就確定屋頂設備的位置與重量，並在雙 T 梁配置圖上標示允許集中荷載區；後續新增設備必須由結構技師檢核。
屋面排水坡度應由支承高程或構件傾斜提供，不應只靠反拱；圖說中標示預估安裝時反拱與允許差值，並要求相鄰雙 T 梁的堆置時間盡量一致。
端部連接應區分哪一端允許滑動、焊接件設計成可容納體積變化，並在圖說中禁止以灌漿填滿承壓墊周圍；缺口內角的裂縫寬度列入定期檢查項目。
連接器配置圖要標示每一個連接器的位置與編號，焊接完成以噴漆或標籤標記並由檢驗人員簽認；未完成連接器的區域不得堆放材料或作為設備通道。
合約與吊裝計畫應把柱底灌漿、端部焊接與翼板焊接列為停止點，規定未完成前不得在上方放置構件，並由結構技師或其指定人員簽認；吊車不得用來調整已放置構件的高程。這些是檢核要求，不是作業許可。
evidenceEn: Structural and services teams should fix rooftop equipment locations and weights early and mark allowable concentrated-load zones on the double-tee layout; any later equipment must be checked by the structural engineer.

Roof drainage slope should come from bearing elevations or sloping members rather than camber alone; drawings should show predicted erection camber and allowable differences, and adjacent tees should have similar storage ages where possible.

End connections should distinguish which end may slide, with welded hardware designed to accommodate volume change, and drawings should forbid grouting solid around bearing pads; crack width at dap corners belongs in periodic inspections.

The connector layout should number every connector, and completed welds are marked with paint or tags and signed by the inspector; no materials may be stockpiled and no equipment may travel over areas with incomplete connectors.

The contract and erection plan should make column-base grouting, end welds and flange welds hold points, prohibiting members above until they are complete, signed off by the structural engineer or a delegate; cranes must not be used to adjust the level of placed members. These are inspection requirements, not operating permits.
pitfalls: 若屋頂設備或增設太陽能板的荷載未納入設計，或排水不良導致積水，腹肋可能出現撓曲裂縫，嚴重時預力鋼絞線屈服；任何一個端部支承失效，整片雙 T 梁就會掉落，因為它沒有其他替代路徑。
缺口內角在多年溫度循環下出現斜裂縫並逐漸擴大，若吊筋不足或錨定不夠，缺口段可能突然剪斷，整片雙 T 梁一端掉落；承壓墊老化或移位使腹肋直接壓在混凝土邊緣，邊緣剝落後擱置長度不足。
為了趕進度而在支承柱尚未灌漿、端部焊接未完成時連續放置大量構件，一個支承失效就引起連鎖倒塌；以吊車而非千斤頂調整墊片，吊鉤勾住吊點把構件拉起，也是 2016 年事故的直接原因之一。
若在混凝土強度不足時提前放鬆，端部底緣壓碎或頂部翼板橫向開裂，裂縫在之後的使用中讓水滲入鋼絞線；脫黏長度錯誤或鋼絞線放鬆順序不對稱，則雙 T 梁側彎或扭曲，安裝時兩腹肋無法同時落在承壓墊上。
長期滲漏讓連接器逐漸鏽斷，平時看不出問題，直到強風或地震時屋頂隔板沿接縫分裂；承壓區剝落使擱置長度不足，極端情況下雙 T 梁一端滑落。
pitfallsEn: If loads from rooftop equipment or added solar panels are left out, or poor drainage lets water pond, the stems can crack in flexure and, in severe cases, strands yield; failure of any single end bearing drops the whole tee, since it has no alternate path.

Diagonal cracks at the dap corner grow over years of thermal cycling, and with too little hanger steel or anchorage the nib can shear off suddenly, dropping one end of the tee; aged or displaced pads let the stem bear directly on the concrete edge, which spalls until seating becomes inadequate.

Placing many members in quick succession while supporting columns are ungrouted and end welds incomplete means one failed support can trigger progressive collapse; using the crane instead of jacks to adjust shims, so that a hook caught a lifting insert and pulled the member up, was one direct cause of the 2016 incident.

Releasing before concrete reaches strength crushes the bottom at the ends or cracks the top flange transversely, and those cracks later admit water to the strands; wrong debonded lengths or an asymmetric release sequence bow or twist the tee so both stems cannot seat on their pads at erection.

Long-term leaks gradually corrode connectors through, showing nothing in normal use until the diaphragm splits along joints in strong wind or an earthquake; spalling at bearings reduces seating length until, in extreme cases, one end of a tee slips off.

guides.scope: 依公開工程原理、官方資料與規範架構編寫的原創教學；步驟是可驗證的學習任務與假想算例，不是設計圖說、施工計畫、吊裝或張拉作業許可，也不是任何專案的設計文件。數值均為教學假設或公開資料，實際工程須由合格技師依規範與實測資料重新計算並簽證。
guides.scopeEn: Original teaching built from public engineering principles, official sources and code frameworks. Steps are verifiable learning tasks and hypothetical exercises, not design drawings, method statements, lifting or stressing permits, or any project's design documents. Numbers are teaching assumptions or public data; real work must be recalculated and certified by qualified engineers using codes and measured data.

guides.concept: 以區劃面積、防火時效、防火門與貫穿填塞、帷幕牆層間防火與樓梯加壓，把高層火災限制在起火區劃並保護結構。數據取自公開資料並經四捨五入，用於學習比較，不是設計值。
guides.conceptEn: Compartment area, fire resistance, fire doors and penetration firestops, curtain-wall perimeter barriers and stair pressurisation that confine high-rise fires to the compartment of origin and protect the structure. Figures come from public sources and are rounded for learning comparisons; they are not design values.

guides.scope: 依公開工程原理、官方資料與規範架構編寫的原創教學；步驟是可驗證的學習任務與假想算例，不是設計圖說、施工計畫、吊裝或張拉作業許可，也不是任何專案的設計文件。數值均為教學假設或公開資料，實際工程須由合格技師依規範與實測資料重新計算並簽證。
guides.scopeEn: Original teaching built from public engineering principles, official sources and code frameworks. Steps are verifiable learning tasks and hypothetical exercises, not design drawings, method statements, lifting or stressing permits, or any project's design documents. Numbers are teaching assumptions or public data; real work must be recalculated and certified by qualified engineers using codes and measured data.

guides.title: 傳力、算例與驗證：高層建築消防分區設計
guides.titleEn: Load paths, calculations and verification: Fire compartmentation in high-rise buildings
guides.concept: 從防火區劃的目的與火載量出發，比較灑水系統與區劃的分工，計算標準火災溫度與時間等效、防火門縫隙的漏煙、樓板邊緣縫隙的等效開口，再處理施工與裝修期間的區劃完整性、耐火試驗、樓梯加壓驗收、區劃失效時的結構臨界溫度，最後談使用管理與交接，並以高雄城中城大樓、倫敦 Grenfell Tower 與費城 One Meridian Plaza 的教訓對照。
guides.conceptEn: Starting from the purpose of compartmentation and fire load, compare the roles of sprinklers and compartments, compute standard-fire temperatures and time equivalence, smoke leakage through fire-door gaps and the equivalent opening of slab-edge gaps, then cover compartment integrity during construction and fit-out, fire-resistance testing, stair-pressurisation acceptance and structural critical temperatures when compartments fail, and finally management in use and handover, compared with lessons from Kaohsiung's Cheng Chung Cheng Building, London's Grenfell Tower and Philadelphia's One Meridian Plaza.
procedure: 防火區劃把建築切成許多以耐火牆、樓板與防火門窗圍成的小盒子，讓火災與煙在一定時間內被限制在起火的盒子裡，爭取避難與消防搶救時間，並限制同時燃燒的面積，保護結構。水平區劃限制每層的燃燒面積，垂直區劃則以樓板、樓梯間與管道間阻止火煙向上蔓延。台灣建築技術規則以每 1,500 m² 為防火構造建築物的區劃原則，設有自動滅火設備時可減計面積；十一層以上樓層則依內裝材料以更小的面積區劃，反映高層救援困難。
室內火災初期以近似時間平方成長，若在閃燃前被灑水系統控制，火勢就不會擴大到整個區劃；區劃則是灑水失效或火勢超出設計時的第二道防線。兩者缺一，風險就大增。1991 年費城 38 層的 One Meridian Plaza 從 22 樓起火，未設灑水的樓層接連燃燒，共燒毀 8 層、歷時超過 19 小時並造成 3 名消防員殉職；火勢直到第一個設有自動灑水的 30 樓才被 10 個灑水頭擋住。
區劃構件的防火時效，是在標準升溫曲線下維持承載、完整性（不讓火焰與熱氣穿過）與隔熱性（背火面溫升不超過限值）的時間。真實火災的強度取決於火載量與開口通風，與標準火災不同，因此工程上常用時間等效的觀念，把真實火災的嚴重度換算成標準火災的等效時間，與構件的防火時效比較。對高層建築而言，樓板同時是結構構件與垂直區劃，防火時效常比一般隔間牆高。
防火門是區劃上最常被打開的缺口：門必須自動關閉並緊密閉合，門框與牆的接縫、門下縫與門扇周邊縫都會漏煙。高層建築的煙囪效應與加壓系統使門兩側存在壓力差，即使只有數公釐的縫隙，也能讓大量煙進入走廊或樓梯。Grenfell Tower 火災中，住戶單元的防火門未能自動關閉與密封，使煙從住戶進入梯廳；事前的防火缺失通知也已列出防火門問題。

高層建築的垂直區劃常在樓板邊緣斷開：帷幕牆與樓板之間留有施工縫，若沒有以經試驗的層間防火填塞封閉，火煙會沿縫隙直接竄上樓。外牆本身也可能成為火的通道，Grenfell Tower 在 2015 至 2016 年改裝時加上鋁複合板與可燃保溫材，火災時火焰沿外牆空腔向上，繞過內部的區劃，約 30 分鐘內抵達屋頂，公開調查第一階段報告指出外牆是火勢快速蔓延的主因。設計上要同時處理樓板邊緣填塞、窗間牆高度與外牆材料的燃燒性。
區劃最大的敵人是施工後期與使用期間的穿孔：機電、弱電、空調與消防管線大量穿越區劃牆與樓板，每一個貫穿部都要以與管材、管徑、牆體型式相符的試驗系統封填。許多填塞在區劃牆完成驗收後才被後續工班打開，或以一般發泡材隨意填補。高層建築的貫穿部以萬計，只要少數失效就足以讓煙在樓層間流通。
區劃構件的防火時效來自標準耐火試驗：把牆、樓板、門或貫穿系統安裝在試驗爐上，依 ISO 834、ASTM E119 或國家標準的升溫曲線加熱，觀察承載力、完整性（有無火焰穿透或棉墊點燃）與隔熱性（背火面平均溫升與最高點溫升）何時失效。試驗結果只適用於試驗構造及其認可的延伸範圍，尺寸、材料、固定方式與試驗不同時，不能直接沿用。台灣內政部建築研究所等機構設有性能試驗設施，支持防火材料與構造的驗證。
高層建築的樓梯與緊急昇降機間是垂直逃生與消防搶救的生命線，常以加壓送風維持比走廊高的壓力，讓門縫只往外漏氣而不讓煙進入。但壓力太高時，門會推不開，避難者無法進入樓梯；壓力太低則擋不住煙。煙囪效應使高層建築上下壓力分布不同，冬夏也不一樣，因此加壓系統要在實際建築中做驗收試驗，確認多扇門同時開啟時仍能維持壓差，且開門力在限值內。
區劃假設火災被限制在一個區劃內燒完，結構防火被覆也依此設計；若灑水與區劃同時失效，多個區劃或多層同時燃燒，熱膨脹與強度折減會同時作用在大範圍的梁、柱與接頭上。One Meridian Plaza 火災後鋼梁與大梁下垂扭曲、樓板開裂，世界貿易中心 7 號大樓則在下層火災失控後倒塌。結構工程師要知道構件在多高的溫度會失去承載力，並與防火被覆的設計溫度一致。
區劃在使用期間最容易被破壞：防火門被撐開、走廊堆放雜物、隔間任意變更、管道間被打開。2021 年 10 月高雄 13 層的城中城大樓火災造成 46 人死亡、41 人受傷，火從一樓起火，因低樓層挑高與玻璃立面迅速竄升，濃煙充滿上方樓層，雜物又助長火勢並阻礙救援，多數死者因吸入濃煙而亡。這類老舊大樓顯示，區劃不只是設計問題，而是管理、檢查與住戶教育的長期責任。
procedureEn: Compartmentation divides a building into boxes enclosed by fire-resisting walls, floors and fire doors and windows, so that fire and smoke stay in the box of origin for a defined time, buying time for evacuation and firefighting and limiting the area burning at once to protect the structure. Horizontal compartments limit the burning area on each floor, while vertical compartmentation uses floors, stair enclosures and shafts to stop upward spread. Taiwan's Building Technical Regulations take 1,500 m² as the basic compartment for fire-resistive buildings, allowing reduced counting where automatic suppression is installed, and require smaller compartments above the 10th floor depending on interior finishes, reflecting the difficulty of high-rise rescue.

Early compartment fires grow roughly with the square of time; if sprinklers control the fire before flashover, it never spreads across the compartment, and compartmentation is the second line of defence if sprinklers fail or the fire exceeds their design. Lose either and risk rises sharply. In 1991 the 38-storey One Meridian Plaza in Philadelphia caught fire on the 22nd floor; unsprinklered floors burned one after another, eight floors were destroyed over more than 19 hours and three firefighters died, and the fire was stopped only on the 30th floor, the first with automatic sprinklers, where ten heads held it back.

The fire resistance of a compartment element is the time it maintains load-bearing capacity, integrity against flames and hot gases and insulation, keeping the unexposed face temperature rise within limits, under the standard temperature–time curve. Real fire severity depends on fire load and ventilation and differs from the standard fire, so engineers use time equivalence to convert real severity into an equivalent standard-fire duration for comparison with the element's rating. In high-rise buildings the floor slab is both a structural member and the vertical compartment, so its rating is often higher than that of ordinary partitions.

Fire doors are the most frequently opened gaps in a compartment: they must self-close and latch tightly, and frame-to-wall joints, undercuts and leaf perimeters all leak smoke. Stack effect and pressurisation in tall buildings create pressure differences across doors, so even gaps of a few millimetres admit large amounts of smoke into corridors or stairs. In the Grenfell Tower fire, flat entrance fire doors failed to close and seal, letting smoke pass from flats into lobbies, and an earlier fire deficiency notice had already listed fire-door problems.

Vertical compartmentation in tall buildings often breaks at the slab edge: a construction gap between curtain wall and floor, if not closed with a tested perimeter fire barrier, lets fire and smoke rise straight up. The façade itself can also become a fire path; Grenfell Tower was overclad in 2015 to 2016 with aluminium composite panels and combustible insulation, and in the fire flames travelled up the external cavity, bypassing internal compartments and reaching the roof within about 30 minutes, with the inquiry's Phase 1 report identifying the exterior as the principal reason for the rapid spread. Design must address slab-edge firestopping, spandrel height and façade combustibility together.

The greatest enemy of compartmentation is late-stage and in-service penetrations: services, data, ductwork and fire-protection pipes cross compartment walls and floors in large numbers, and each penetration must be sealed with a tested system matching pipe material, size and wall type. Many seals are opened by later trades after the wall has been accepted, or patched with ordinary foam. A high-rise building has tens of thousands of penetrations, and a small fraction failing is enough to let smoke circulate between floors.

An element's fire rating comes from standard fire-resistance tests: a wall, floor, door or penetration system is mounted on a furnace and heated to the ISO 834, ASTM E119 or national curve while load-bearing capacity, integrity (flame penetration or cotton-pad ignition) and insulation (average and maximum temperature rise on the unexposed face) are watched for failure. Results apply only to the tested construction and its approved field of extension; different sizes, materials or fixings cannot simply borrow the rating. Institutions such as Taiwan's Architecture and Building Research Institute operate performance test facilities that support verification of fire-resisting materials and constructions.

Stairs and fire-fighting lift lobbies in tall buildings are the lifelines for vertical escape and firefighting, often pressurised above corridor pressure so that air leaks outward through door gaps and smoke stays out. Too much pressure makes doors impossible to open and occupants cannot enter the stair; too little fails to hold back smoke. Stack effect distributes pressure differently over the height and between winter and summer, so pressurisation must be acceptance-tested in the real building to confirm that the pressure difference holds with several doors open and that door-opening forces stay within limits.

Compartmentation assumes a fire burns out within one compartment, and structural fire protection is designed accordingly; if sprinklers and compartments both fail, several compartments or floors burn at once, and thermal expansion and strength loss act together on beams, columns and connections over a wide area. After the One Meridian Plaza fire, steel beams and girders sagged and twisted and floors cracked, while World Trade Center 7 collapsed after lower-floor fires burned uncontrolled. Structural engineers must know the temperature at which members lose capacity and align it with the fireproofing design temperature.

Compartments are most easily defeated in use: fire doors propped open, corridors cluttered, partitions altered at will and shafts opened. The October 2021 fire at Kaohsiung's 13-storey Cheng Chung Cheng Building killed 46 people and injured 41; starting on the ground floor, it rose quickly through high-ceilinged lower floors with a glass frontage and filled the floors above with smoke, while clutter fed the fire and blocked rescue, and most victims died of smoke inhalation. Such ageing buildings show that compartmentation is not only a design issue but a long-term responsibility of management, inspection and occupant education.
evidence: 防火區劃圖應由建築師與消防、結構、機電專業共同簽認，並作為竣工交接文件的一部分；任何隔間變更都必須回到這張圖上檢討。
業主與管理單位應把灑水系統、消防泵、立管減壓閥與緊急電源列為同一套維護與測試計畫，任何停水或停用都要事前通報並採取補償措施，例如加強巡查與臨時滅火設備。
防火構造的材料送審要附耐火試驗報告與構造詳圖，現場依詳圖施作並由監造逐區查驗；使用用途改變為高火載量時，須重新檢討防火時效。
管理規約應禁止撐開防火門，需要常開者必須改為與偵測器連動的自動關閉裝置；防火門的五金更換須使用經認證的配件，並列入定期檢查表。
帷幕牆、防火填塞與結構三方要在施工圖階段協調樓板邊緣細部，層間填塞列為帷幕牆安裝每層的停止點；外牆材料變更必須提出燃燒性證明並經審查，地震後檢查表應包含層間填塞。
evidenceEn: The compartmentation plan should be signed jointly by the architect and the fire, structural and services disciplines and form part of the handover documents; any partition change must be reviewed against it.

Owners and managers should treat sprinklers, fire pumps, standpipe pressure-reducing valves and emergency power as one maintenance and testing programme, notifying any shutdown in advance and adopting compensating measures such as extra patrols and temporary extinguishing equipment.

Submittals for fire-resisting construction must include fire test reports and construction details, with site work following the details and inspected area by area; any change to a high-fire-load use requires the ratings to be reassessed.

House rules should forbid propping fire doors open, with doors that must stay open fitted with detector-linked automatic release; door hardware replacements must use certified components and be included in periodic inspections.

Curtain-wall, firestopping and structural teams must coordinate slab-edge details at shop-drawing stage, with perimeter barriers a hold point on every floor of curtain-wall installation; any façade material change requires combustibility evidence and review, and post-earthquake checklists should include perimeter barriers.
pitfalls: 若區劃線在平面上看似完整，但在天花板上方、架高地板下方或帷幕牆邊緣斷開，火煙會繞過區劃牆擴散，使整層甚至多層同時受害；以灑水系統放大區劃面積後，若灑水系統失效，燃燒面積就超過結構與救援的假設。
若現場以未經試驗的輕隔間或板材替代，或固定間距、板材層數與試驗不同，區劃牆在火災中提早失去完整性；倉儲或資料中心等高火載量用途若沿用辦公室的時間等效，真實火災會超過構件的防火時效。
層間填塞因帷幕牆變位或施工擠壓脫落，或保溫材被替換為可燃材料，火災時火煙沿樓板邊緣與外牆空腔逐層向上，區劃形同虛設；地震後帷幕牆層間變位也可能把填塞拉開而無人發現。
若引用的試驗報告是較小尺寸的門或較薄的牆，現場大尺寸構造在火災中翹曲變形、提早出現縫隙；把非承重試驗的牆當作承重區劃牆使用，火災中可能因承載而提早倒塌。
若防火被覆依一般使用率設計，而某些構件因設計變更或增加荷載使用率提高，臨界溫度下降，同樣厚度的被覆在火災中提早失效；機電施工刮除或撞落被覆而未修補，也會形成局部弱點。
pitfallsEn: Compartment lines that look complete on plan but break above ceilings, below raised floors or at the curtain-wall edge let fire and smoke bypass the walls and involve whole floors or several floors at once; once sprinklers justify larger compartments, sprinkler failure leaves a burning area beyond what structure and rescue assumed.

Substituting untested partitions or boards on site, or changing fixing spacing or board layers from the tested build-up, makes compartment walls lose integrity early in a fire; applying office time equivalence to high-fire-load uses such as storage or data centres lets real fires exceed element ratings.

Perimeter barriers dislodged by curtain-wall movement or construction, or insulation swapped for combustible products, let fire and smoke climb floor by floor along slab edges and façade cavities, nullifying compartmentation; storey drift in an earthquake can also pull barriers open unnoticed.

Citing a test on a smaller door or thinner wall means larger site constructions bow and open gaps early in a fire; using a wall tested as non-load-bearing as a load-bearing compartment wall can lead to early collapse under load in a fire.

If fireproofing is sized for typical utilisation while design changes or added loads raise utilisation in some members, their critical temperature falls and the same coating fails early in a fire; fireproofing scraped or knocked off by services work and not repaired creates local weak points.

guides.title: 工程檔案：關鍵數據、年代、規範與案例
guides.titleEn: Engineering dossier: key figures, timeline, codes and landmarks
guides.concept: 以臨界溫度、斷面係數與現場厚度、密度、黏結抽驗，確保鋼構件在火害中維持設計耐火時效。數據取自公開資料並經四捨五入，用於學習比較，不是設計值。
guides.conceptEn: Critical temperature, section factor and field thickness, density and bond checks that keep steel members within their rated fire resistance. Figures come from public sources and are rounded for learning comparisons; they are not design values.
facts: ASTM E119 對梁的溫度判準為四點平均 1,100°F（593°C）或任一點 1,300°F（704°C）
IBC 規定 SFRM 黏結強度一般至少 150 psf（約 7.2 kPa），樓高 75–420 ft 高層為 430 psf，超過 420 ft 為 1,000 psf
標準密度 SFRM 約 15–21 pcf（240–336 kg/m³），中密度約 22–39 pcf
世界貿易中心樓板桁架 1969 年規定被覆 1/2 in，1995 年升級規定為 1.5 in，NIST 引用實測平均約 0.75 in 與 2.5 in
NIST 委託 UL 做了 4 次 ASTM E119 樓板試驗，分別在 17 ft 與 35 ft 試驗爐進行
紐約時報大樓約 250,000 ft² 外露鋼構以 80 或 120 mils 環氧膨脹漆保護，要求至少 2 小時
薄塗型膨脹漆約在 200–250°C 開始反應，膨脹比約 50 倍
Cardington 1995–1997 年試驗中，未保護鋼梁最高約 1,100°C 而結構未倒塌
馬德里溫莎大樓為 30 層，2005 年火災延燒約 1¾ 小時後上部外圍局部崩塌
factsEn: ASTM E119 beam criteria: 1,100°F (593°C) average over four thermocouples or 1,300°F (704°C) at any point
IBC requires SFRM bond strength of at least 150 psf (about 7.2 kPa), 430 psf for 75–420 ft high-rises and 1,000 psf above 420 ft
Standard-density SFRM is about 15–21 pcf (240–336 kg/m³); medium density is about 22–39 pcf
World Trade Center floor trusses were specified 1/2 in of fireproofing in 1969 and 1.5 in for the 1995 upgrade; NIST cited measured averages of about 0.75 in and 2.5 in
NIST commissioned 4 ASTM E119 floor tests from UL, in 17 ft and 35 ft furnaces
About 250,000 ft² of exposed steel at the New York Times Building was protected with 80 or 120 mils of epoxy intumescent for at least 2 hours
Thin-film intumescents start reacting at about 200–250°C and expand about 50-fold
In the 1995–1997 Cardington tests unprotected steel beams reached about 1,100°C without structural collapse
The Windsor Building in Madrid had 30 storeys; in the 2005 fire its upper perimeter partly collapsed after about 1¾ hours of severe burning
timeline: 1918　ASTM 委員會通過建築構造耐火試驗標準並建立標準升溫曲線
1969　紐約港務局函文規定世界貿易中心樓板桁架噴覆被覆 1/2 in
1995–1997　英國 Cardington 實尺寸鋼構火災試驗，未保護鋼梁未導致倒塌
2005　馬德里溫莎大樓於被覆改修期間發生火災，上部外圍鋼柱失效
2007　紐約時報大樓完工，外露鋼構採現場噴塗環氧膨脹型防火塗料
2007–2009　ICC 依 NIST 建議提高 SFRM 黏結強度並納入現場特別檢驗，見於 2009 年版 IBC
timelineEn: 1918 — An ASTM committee adopts a fire-test standard for building construction and establishes the standard time–temperature curve
1969 — A Port Authority letter specifies 1/2 in of sprayed fireproofing for World Trade Center floor trusses
1995–1997 — Full-scale Cardington steel-frame fire tests in the UK show unprotected beams without collapse
2005 — The Windsor Building in Madrid burns mid-retrofit and its upper perimeter steel columns fail
2007 — The New York Times Building is completed with site-sprayed epoxy intumescent on its exposed steel
2007–2009 — ICC adopts NIST-based SFRM bond and special-inspection requirements, reflected in the 2009 IBC

guides.title: 傳力、算例與驗證：鋼構耐火被覆施工
guides.titleEn: Load paths, calculations and verification: Structural-steel fireproofing application
guides.concept: 從鋼材在火害中的強度折減與臨界溫度出發，建立斷面係數與被覆厚度的熱傳關係，比較噴覆型防火材料（SFRM）與膨脹型防火塗料的材料機制、施工環境與交叉作業損傷，再以 ASTM E605／E736 現場抽驗、耐火試驗登錄與約束條件判讀完成驗收，並以世界貿易中心、紐約時報大樓與馬德里溫莎大樓說明厚度、黏結與改修過渡期的風險。
guides.conceptEn: Starting from steel strength loss and critical temperature in fire, build the heat-transfer link between section factor and protection thickness, compare the mechanisms, site conditions and trade damage of sprayed fire-resistive materials (SFRM) and intumescent coatings, then close acceptance with ASTM E605/E736 field sampling, fire-test listings and restraint classification, using the World Trade Center, the New York Times Building and the Windsor Building in Madrid to show the risks of thin spots, weak bond and half-finished retrofits.
procedure: 結構鋼在約 400°C 以上開始明顯損失降伏強度與彈性模數，600°C 左右只剩常溫強度的一半左右，而一般建築火災的煙層溫度在數十分鐘內即可超過 800°C。耐火被覆本身不承載，它的任務是延緩熱量進入鋼材，使構件在要求的耐火時效內仍低於「臨界溫度」，也就是剩餘強度恰好等於火災時載重效應的溫度。臨界溫度不是固定值：火災載重組合採用較低的活載重，構件利用率越低，可容許的溫度越高；梁柱的支承與約束條件也會改變破壞模式。
受火鋼材的升溫速度取決於吸熱表面積與可儲熱鋼材體積之比，也就是斷面係數 Ap/V（美制以每呎重量與受熱周長之比 W/D 表示，意義相反）。同樣的被覆厚度包在薄腹細長斷面上升溫較快，包在厚重斷面上升溫較慢。被覆以低熱傳導係數形成熱阻，熱流大約與厚度成反比；含水的水泥系材料在約 100°C 時還會因水分蒸發出現升溫平台。三面受火（上方為樓板）與四面受火的周長不同，必須依實際構造計算。
SFRM 以石膏或水泥為膠結材，加入礦物纖維、蛭石或輕質骨材，濕噴或乾噴於鋼材表面，固化後形成多孔隔熱層。標準密度產品（約 15–21 pcf，240–336 kg/m³）適用於隱蔽空間；中、高密度產品抗衝擊與黏結較佳，用於停車場、機房或外露區。耐火試驗只對特定試體斷面取得厚度，其他斷面須以經認可的換算式調整：較重的斷面（W/D 較大）吸熱能力較高，可用較薄的被覆，但不得低於登錄的最小厚度。
膨脹型防火塗料在常溫下只是一層數百微米到數毫米的塗膜，受熱到約 200–250°C 時，酸源、碳源與發泡劑反應，膨脹成多孔炭化層；薄塗型膨脹比可達約 50 倍，厚塗環氧型膨脹較小但耐候與抗衝擊較佳，常用於建築師希望保留鋼構外形的外露梁柱。塗膜是一個系統：底漆提供防蝕與附著，膨脹層提供耐火，面漆提供耐候與顏色；三者必須在試驗中一起驗證，任意更換底漆或面漆都可能讓炭化層剝落或膨脹不足。
被覆能否在火災時留在鋼材上，首先取決於施工當天的表面與環境：油汙、軋鋼鱗片、浮鏽或不相容的底漆會降低黏結，結露的鋼面會讓塗膜附著不良，低溫則使水泥系材料無法正常水化。SFRM 通常在樓板混凝土澆置、鋼承板與吊架夾具完成後施作，以免後續焊接或鑽孔破壞被覆；但若太晚，管線與風管已擋住鋼梁，噴槍無法到達。施工順序因此是品質的一部分，而不只是進度問題。
被覆完成後，機電、消防灑水、天花板與帷幕牆工班仍需在鋼梁上固定吊架、切割或搬運材料，常刮除或撞落局部被覆。由於熱流近似與厚度成反比，局部變薄或裸露的區域就是熱的捷徑，使該處鋼材升溫遠快於平均厚度所預測。NIST 在世界貿易中心調查中以「熱等效均勻厚度」描述不均勻被覆的實際效果：原設計的平均厚度並不能代表最薄處的風險。
現場驗收把試驗室的耐火設計轉成三個可量測的量：厚度、密度與黏結強度。厚度依 ASTM E605 以探針式量規在指定位置量測，梁與柱都有規定的點數與抽樣比例；密度由切取試塊的體積與乾重求得；黏結強度則依 ASTM E736 以拉拔試驗確認被覆不會從鋼材或自身內部分離。美國 IBC 要求這些項目由特別檢驗員執行，並依樓高提高高層建築的黏結強度門檻。
ASTM E119（與 UL 263 同等）以標準升溫曲線加熱載重試體，梁的溫度判準為四點平均 593°C 或任一點 704°C；試驗結果以登錄設計公告，規定鋼材斷面、被覆產品、厚度與構造細部。試驗分為約束與非約束兩種等級：約束假設周邊結構阻止梁受熱伸長，會在梁內產生軸壓並改變破壞模式。實際建築的約束程度介於兩者之間，熱膨脹推擠柱與接頭本身也是火災倒塌的重要機制。
室內乾燥環境中的 SFRM 數十年幾乎不變，但外露或半外露構件要承受雨水、紫外線、溫濕循環與鹽分。薄塗型膨脹漆吸濕後可能失去膨脹能力，因此外露鋼構多採厚塗環氧型膨脹漆加耐候面漆；紐約時報大樓外露的角柱與橫梁即以約 80 或 120 mils（約 2 或 3 mm）的環氧膨脹漆一次噴塗，再滾平外觀。防火塗層同時擔任防蝕層，一旦面漆破損或膜下鏽蝕擴展，耐火與防蝕會一起失效。

既有鋼構建築常因法規更新、樓高分類或用途變更而需提高耐火時效，改修期間建築多半仍在使用，部分樓層已完成、部分尚未施作，防火區劃與被覆同時處於不完整狀態。馬德里溫莎大樓 2005 年火災時，外圍鋼柱的補強被覆只完成到第 17 層以下，未保護的上部外圍鋼柱在火中失效，上方樓層局部崩塌；世界貿易中心在 1990 年代把樓板桁架被覆由 1/2 in 提高到 1.5 in，也只完成部分樓層。改修計畫必須同時管控過渡期風險。
procedureEn: Structural steel begins to lose yield strength and stiffness noticeably above about 400°C and keeps only about half its ambient strength near 600°C, while gas temperatures in an ordinary building fire can exceed 800°C within tens of minutes. Fireproofing carries no load; its task is to slow heat flow into the steel so that, for the required fire-resistance period, the member stays below its critical temperature, the temperature at which the remaining strength just equals the load effect in fire. That temperature is not fixed: fire load combinations use reduced live load, a lower utilisation allows a higher temperature, and support and restraint conditions change the failure mode.

The heating rate of protected steel depends on the ratio of heated surface to the steel volume that stores heat, the section factor Ap/V (US practice uses weight per foot over heated perimeter, W/D, the inverse sense). The same protection thickness lets a thin-walled slender section heat faster than a heavy one. The protection forms a thermal resistance with low conductivity, so heat flow is roughly inversely proportional to thickness; moisture in cementitious products also produces a temperature plateau near 100°C as water evaporates. Three-sided exposure under a slab and four-sided exposure give different perimeters and must follow the actual construction.

SFRM uses a gypsum or cement binder with mineral fibre, vermiculite or lightweight aggregate, sprayed wet or dry onto the steel and cured into a porous insulating layer. Standard-density products (about 15–21 pcf, 240–336 kg/m³) suit concealed spaces; medium- and high-density products resist impact and bond better and are used in car parks, plant rooms or exposed areas. A fire test establishes thickness only for the tested section, so other sections are adjusted with an accepted substitution equation: heavier sections with higher W/D absorb more heat and may take a thinner coat, but never below the listed minimum thickness.

An intumescent coating is only a film of a few hundred microns to a few millimetres at ambient temperature; at about 200–250°C its acid source, carbon source and blowing agent react and swell into a porous char. Thin-film products can expand about 50 times, while thick-film epoxy types expand less but resist weather and impact better; they are used where architects want exposed beams and columns to keep their steel profile. The film is a system: the primer gives corrosion protection and adhesion, the intumescent layer gives fire resistance and the topcoat gives weathering and colour. All three must be proven together in testing, and swapping a primer or topcoat can make the char detach or under-expand.

Whether protection stays on the steel in a fire depends first on the surface and ambient conditions on the day of application: oil, mill scale, loose rust or an incompatible primer reduce bond, condensation on the steel prevents coating adhesion, and low temperature stops cementitious products from hydrating properly. SFRM is normally applied after the slab is cast and deck attachments and hanger clips are installed, so that later welding or drilling does not damage it; but if it comes too late, pipes and ducts already shield the beams and the spray gun cannot reach. Sequencing is therefore part of quality, not just of programme.

After fireproofing, MEP, sprinkler, ceiling and façade trades still fix hangers to beams and cut or move materials, often scraping or knocking off local patches. Because heat flow is roughly inversely proportional to thickness, thin or bare spots become thermal short cuts where the steel heats much faster than the average thickness predicts. In its World Trade Center investigation NIST described the real effect of uneven protection with a thermally equivalent uniform thickness: the average thickness does not represent the risk at the thinnest areas.

Field acceptance turns the laboratory fire design into three measurable quantities: thickness, density and bond strength. Thickness is measured to ASTM E605 with a probe gauge at prescribed locations, with set numbers of readings and sampling rates for beams and columns; density comes from the volume and dry mass of cut samples; and bond strength is checked to ASTM E736 with a pull-off test showing that the material does not separate from the steel or within itself. The US IBC assigns these items to a special inspector and raises the bond threshold for high-rise buildings by height.

ASTM E119, equivalent to UL 263, heats loaded specimens along a standard time–temperature curve; for beams the temperature criteria are 593°C averaged over four thermocouples or 704°C at any point. Results are published as listed designs that fix the steel section, protection product, thickness and construction details. Tests yield restrained and unrestrained ratings: restraint assumes the surrounding structure prevents thermal elongation of the beam, inducing axial compression and changing the failure mode. Real buildings fall between the two, and thermal expansion pushing on columns and connections is itself an important collapse mechanism.

SFRM in dry interiors hardly changes for decades, but exposed or semi-exposed members face rain, ultraviolet light, thermal and humidity cycling and salt. Thin-film intumescents can lose their ability to expand after absorbing moisture, so exterior steel usually takes a thick-film epoxy intumescent with a weathering topcoat; the exposed corner columns and cross beams of the New York Times Building received epoxy intumescent sprayed in one coat at about 80 or 120 mils, about 2 or 3 mm, and back-rolled for appearance. The fire coating also acts as corrosion protection, so once the topcoat fails or rust creeps beneath the film, fire and corrosion protection fail together.

Existing steel buildings often need higher fire ratings after code updates, a change of height class or a change of use, and they usually stay occupied during the work, so some floors are finished and others not, with compartmentation and protection both incomplete. When the Windsor Building in Madrid burned in 2005, retrofit protection to the perimeter steel columns had been completed only below the 17th floor; the unprotected upper perimeter columns failed and upper storeys partly collapsed. The World Trade Center raised floor-truss protection from 1/2 in to 1.5 in in the 1990s, but only on some floors. A retrofit plan must manage the risk of the transition period.
evidence: 設計圖應以表格列出每種構件的耐火時效、所依據的試驗登錄編號、利用率假設與所需厚度，並註明「變更斷面或載重須重新核算被覆」；這張表是監造、被覆廠商與檢驗員共同的依據。
深化圖階段由鋼構廠輸出每支構件的斷面係數清單，被覆廠商據此提出逐件厚度表並簽章；現場每支構件以噴漆或標籤標示所需厚度，讓施作人員與檢驗員不必在現場自行換算。
規範應依區域指定密度等級（外露區與停車場用中、高密度），並要求廠商提交產品登錄、替代計算與現場密度試驗計畫；任何以較薄厚度取代設計值的提案，都須經結構與防火設計者書面同意。
工廠塗裝與現場塗裝要劃清界面：哪些構件在廠內完成、運輸吊裝損傷由誰修補、接合部位留白多少與如何補塗，都要寫入塗裝計畫；底漆或面漆變更須取得塗料廠商的相容性書面確認。
把被覆前檢查設為停止點：鋼承板焊接、吊架夾具、剪力釘與穿孔全部完成，表面與環境紀錄合格後，由監造簽發被覆許可；之後任何焊接或鑽孔都要事先申請，並排定補修與複驗。
evidenceEn: Drawings should tabulate for each member type the fire-resistance rating, the listing number relied on, the assumed utilisation and the required thickness, with a note that any change of section or load requires the fireproofing to be re-checked; this table is the common reference for the supervising engineer, applicator and inspector.

At shop-drawing stage the steel fabricator issues a section-factor list for every member, the fireproofing contractor returns a signed member-by-member thickness schedule, and each member on site is marked with its required thickness so that applicators and inspectors never recalculate in the field.

The specification should assign density classes by zone, with medium or high density for exposed areas and car parks, and require listings, substitution calculations and a field density-testing plan; any proposal to use a thinner coat than designed needs written approval from the structural and fire designers.

Draw a clear line between shop and site application: which members are finished in the shop, who repairs transport and erection damage, how much is left bare at connections and how it is made good must all be in the coating plan; any primer or topcoat change needs the coating manufacturer's written compatibility confirmation.

Make the pre-fireproofing inspection a hold point: deck welding, hanger clips, shear studs and penetrations all complete and surface and ambient records accepted, then the supervising engineer issues a permit to fireproof; any later welding or drilling requires a prior request and scheduled repair and re-inspection.
pitfalls: 把所有構件一律套用相同被覆厚度而不看利用率與斷面，常造成重載的細長柱保護不足、輕載大梁卻過度保護；火災中保護不足的柱先達臨界溫度並縮短，迫使上方樓層荷重重分配，嚴重時引發連鎖破壞。
把梁的替代式用在柱，或為較輕斷面減少厚度，等於拿試驗沒有涵蓋的條件冒險；把標準密度產品噴在經常受碰撞的停車場或機房，短期內就被撞落、刮除，留下大片裸露鋼材。
在潮濕清晨噴塗膨脹漆，膜下結露造成大面積起泡剝離；SFRM 噴在帶油的鋼梁上，乾燥後看似完整，卻在後續振動或碰撞時整塊脫落。若被覆完成後才在梁上焊接吊架，熱影響區的被覆燒損又常被天花板遮住而未被發現。
只量容易到達的腹板而不量下翼板邊緣，或讓遠超設計的讀值拉高平均，都會掩蓋薄點。世界貿易中心樓板桁架原規定 1/2 in，NIST 引用的實測平均約 0.75 in、變異係數約 0.4；若以常態分布估算，約兩成讀值可能低於 0.5 in。
把室內型薄塗膨脹漆用於半外露的雨遮梁或停車場邊梁，數年後塗膜吸濕軟化、起泡，火災時膨脹不足；邊緣與螺栓頭等銳角處膜厚最薄，往往最先鏽蝕並從底部把塗層撐開。
pitfallsEn: Applying one thickness to every member regardless of utilisation and section often leaves heavily loaded slender columns under-protected and lightly loaded girders over-protected; in a fire the under-protected column reaches its critical temperature first and shortens, forcing load redistribution in the floors above and, at worst, progressive failure.

Using the beam equation for columns, or reducing thickness for a lighter section, gambles on conditions the test never covered; spraying standard-density product in a car park or plant room that sees frequent impact soon leaves it knocked off and scraped away, exposing large areas of bare steel.

Intumescent sprayed on a damp morning with condensation under the film blisters and peels over large areas; SFRM sprayed on oily beams looks intact once dry but falls off in sheets under later vibration or impact. Hangers welded to beams after fireproofing burn the protection in the heat-affected zone, and the damage is often hidden by the ceiling and never found.

Measuring only the easily reached web and not the bottom-flange edges, or letting very thick readings inflate the average, hides thin spots. The World Trade Center floor trusses originally specified 1/2 in, and NIST cited a measured average of about 0.75 in with a coefficient of variation of about 0.4; a normal-distribution estimate puts about one reading in five below 0.5 in.

Using an interior thin-film intumescent on semi-exposed canopy or car-park edge beams lets the film absorb moisture, soften and blister within a few years, so it under-expands in a fire; sharp edges and bolt heads carry the thinnest film and are often the first to corrode and lift the coating from beneath.

guides.scopeEn: Original teaching built from public engineering principles, official sources and code frameworks. Steps are verifiable learning tasks and hypothetical exercises, not design drawings, method statements, lifting or stressing permits, or any project's design documents. Numbers are teaching assumptions or public data; real work must be recalculated and certified by qualified engineers using codes and measured data.

pitfalls: 把四捨五入的公開數據當成設計值或允收值使用。
沒有確認規範版本、適用地區與荷載組合就直接套用另一國的條文。
pitfallsEn: Using rounded public figures as design or acceptance values.
Applying another country's clauses without checking edition, jurisdiction and load combinations.

guides.title: 傳力、算例與驗證：大型玻璃肋結構安裝
guides.titleEn: Load paths, calculations and verification: Structural glass-fin installation
guides.concept: 從全玻璃立面的風壓傳遞路徑出發，把面玻璃視為支承於玻璃肋之間的板，再把玻璃肋當作細長深梁檢核面內應力、撓度與側向扭轉挫屈，說明膠合中間膜、強化與熱浸處理、結構矽利康與埋入式金屬件的設計要點，最後處理長玻璃的運輸翻轉、頂部滑動接頭、實體試驗、熱應力與自爆風險，並以上海陸家嘴、曼谷 Iconsiam 與紐約第五大道蘋果直營店的公開工程資料比較不同做法。
guides.conceptEn: Starting from the wind load path through an all-glass façade, treat the face glass as plates spanning between fins and each fin as a slender deep beam checked for in-plane stress, deflection and lateral–torsional buckling, then cover laminated interlayers, toughening and heat soaking, structural silicone and laminated-in metal fittings, and finally long-glass transport and tilting, sliding head joints, physical testing, thermal stress and spontaneous-breakage risk, comparing approaches through public engineering information on Apple Pudong in Shanghai, Apple Iconsiam in Bangkok and Apple Fifth Avenue in New York.
procedure: 全玻璃立面沒有鋁或鋼豎框，面玻璃把風壓以板彎曲傳到兩側的玻璃肋，玻璃肋再以面內彎曲把荷重送到頂部與底部的主結構。玻璃肋垂直於立面放置，就像一支立起來的深梁：深度方向抵抗風壓彎矩，厚度方向卻很薄。面玻璃與玻璃肋通常以結構矽利康黏結，或以金屬夾具、埋入式金屬件連接；面玻璃的自重則多由底部墊塊或頂部吊掛承受，不經過矽利康。設計時要分清楚每一種荷重走哪一條路徑，否則某個看似次要的接合會意外承擔主要力量。
玻璃肋的深厚比常超過 10，面內彎曲時受壓的那一條邊像一根細長壓桿，可能側向彎出並帶動整支肋扭轉，這就是側向扭轉挫屈。風壓與風吸使受壓邊在內側與外側之間交替：若受壓邊緊貼面玻璃並由矽利康連續拘束，挫屈長度大幅縮短；若受壓邊是室內側的自由邊，就只能靠肋本身的弱軸與扭轉勁度抵抗。玻璃是脆性材料，挫屈造成的附加應力會直接疊加在邊緣，常在達到彎曲強度前就破壞。

結構玻璃肋幾乎都是兩片以上的膠合玻璃，中間夾 PVB 或離子型（ionoplast）中間膜。面內彎曲時各片玻璃深度相同、共同變形，中間膜幾乎不影響強度；但弱軸彎曲、扭轉與挫屈時，各片能否像一塊厚板一起作用，取決於中間膜的剪力勁度，而這個勁度會隨溫度升高與荷重持續時間變長而急劇下降。因此陣風、長期風或日照高溫下的同一支肋，可能有完全不同的有效厚度。離子型中間膜在較高溫度下保有較高剪力勁度，也讓玻璃破裂後的殘餘承載較好。
面玻璃與玻璃肋的接合有兩大做法：以結構矽利康連續黏結，讓風壓沿整條邊均勻傳遞；或以螺栓、夾具與膠合入玻璃的金屬件集中傳力。矽利康柔軟、可吸收溫差與微小變位，但設計應力很低，咬合寬度與厚度都要計算；螺栓孔則會在孔緣造成應力集中，必須以襯套、墊片與強化玻璃處理。膠合入玻璃的金屬件讓力量分散到中間膜與多片玻璃，減少外露夾具與鑽孔數量，是近年大型玻璃結構的重要發展。
十公尺以上的玻璃肋與面玻璃需要特殊運輸架、吊具與現場動線；玻璃最脆弱的時刻往往不是使用期，而是平放、翻轉與吊起的過程。玻璃肋平放時以弱軸受自重彎曲，與設計時的強軸受力完全不同，若支點位置不當，搬運應力可能接近風壓設計應力；邊緣碰撞造成的小缺口更是日後破裂的起點。因此吊裝計畫要指定支點位置、翻轉方式（立式運輸架或翻轉架）、吸盤或夾具配置、風速限制與每一步的停止條件。
玻璃肋安裝的關鍵是讓它只承擔設計中的荷重，而不被主結構的變形「擠壓」。屋頂梁在活載重、雪或溫度下會上下變位，若玻璃肋頂部固定死，就會被當成柱子受壓；因此常見做法是底部固定、頂部只傳遞水平力並允許垂直滑動，或改為頂部吊掛、底部滑動，讓玻璃處於受拉。安裝順序通常是先定位支座、立起並調整玻璃肋垂直度，再裝面玻璃、最後施打矽利康，每一步都要量測累積公差。
玻璃結構的計算對邊界條件、中間膜耦合與接合剛度非常敏感，因此大型玻璃肋常以實尺寸樣品做載重試驗：在試驗架上以分級靜載重或氣壓箱施加設計風壓與超載，量測撓度、側向位移與殘餘變形，並在破壞試驗中觀察裂紋起點與破裂後行為。實測撓度若明顯大於計算，表示支承鬆動、耦合不足或接合滑移，必須在量產前找出原因。
玻璃破裂幾乎都從邊緣或孔緣開始，因此現場檢查的重點是邊緣：研磨等級、崩邊、刮傷與接觸金屬。局部遮陽、室內暖氣出風口或深色貼紙會讓同一片玻璃中央與邊緣溫差擴大，在邊緣產生拉應力；未強化或邊緣受損的玻璃最容易因熱應力破裂。強化玻璃還要檢查應力分布是否均勻（以偏光觀察）與輥筒波紋等光學缺陷，後者雖不影響安全，卻常是業主驗收爭議的來源。
強化玻璃內若含硫化鎳雜質，雜質在常溫下會緩慢相變並體積膨脹，數年後可能讓玻璃在沒有外力的情況下突然破裂，這就是自爆。熱浸處理（如 EN 14179）把強化後的玻璃加熱並保持一段時間，讓含雜質的玻璃在工廠先破，以降低現場自爆機率，但無法完全消除。玻璃肋若為強化玻璃，自爆一片就要靠其餘玻璃與中間膜承擔；長期而言，中間膜邊緣受潮脫層、矽利康老化與金屬件腐蝕也會削弱接合。
大型玻璃肋的設計壽命可達數十年，但必須預期至少一次更換：自爆、撞擊或改裝都可能需要拆下單支肋或單片面玻璃。更換時玻璃肋是結構構件，拆除前需臨時支撐面玻璃並傳遞風壓，因此設計時就要預留吊點、運輸路徑與替換玻璃的尺寸限制。紐約第五大道蘋果直營店的玻璃立方體在 2011 年改建時，以更少、更大的玻璃單元與更少的接合件取代原版，正說明減少接合數量能同時降低維護與更換的工作量。
procedureEn: An all-glass façade has no aluminium or steel mullions: face glass carries wind pressure by plate bending to the fins on either side, and each fin carries the load by in-plane bending to the main structure at its top and bottom. A fin stands perpendicular to the façade like an upended deep beam, resisting the wind moment through its depth while being very thin through its thickness. Face glass and fins are usually joined with structural silicone, or with metal clamps and laminated-in fittings, while the self-weight of the face glass sits on setting blocks at the base or hangs from the head, not on the silicone. The designer must know which path each load takes, or a seemingly minor joint ends up carrying a major force.

A glass fin often has a depth-to-thickness ratio above 10, so under in-plane bending its compressed edge behaves like a slender strut that can bow sideways and twist the whole fin, which is lateral–torsional buckling. Wind pressure and suction alternate the compressed edge between the inside and outside: if the compressed edge bears against face glass with continuous silicone restraint, the buckling length shrinks sharply; if it is the free inner edge, only the fin's own weak-axis and torsional stiffness resist. Glass is brittle, so the extra stress from buckling adds directly at the edge and often breaks the fin before its bending strength is reached.

Structural fins are almost always laminates of two or more plies with a PVB or ionoplast interlayer. Under in-plane bending all plies have the same depth and deform together, so the interlayer barely affects strength; but in weak-axis bending, torsion and buckling, whether the plies act as one thick plate depends on the interlayer's shear stiffness, which drops sharply with higher temperature and longer load duration. The same fin can therefore have very different effective thickness under a gust, a sustained wind or hot sunshine. Ionoplast interlayers keep more shear stiffness at higher temperatures and also give better residual capacity after the glass breaks.

Face glass joins fins in two main ways: continuous structural silicone bonding, which transfers wind evenly along the whole edge, or bolts, clamps and laminated-in metal fittings that transfer it at points. Silicone is soft and absorbs thermal and small movements, but its design stress is very low, so bite and thickness must be calculated; bolt holes concentrate stress at the hole edge and need bushings, liners and toughened glass. Metal fittings laminated into the glass spread force through the interlayer and several plies, reducing exposed clamps and drilled holes, an important recent development in large glass structures.

Fins and face panels longer than ten metres need special transport frames, lifting gear and site routes; glass is often most vulnerable not in service but while lying flat, being tilted and being lifted. A fin lying flat bends under its own weight about the weak axis, completely unlike its strong-axis design loading, and with poorly placed supports the handling stress can approach the wind design stress; small chips from edge impact become the origin of later breakage. The lifting plan must therefore specify support positions, the tilting method (upright transport frame or tilting frame), vacuum-pad or clamp layout, wind-speed limits and stop conditions for every step.

The key to fin installation is that the fin carries only its design loads and is never squeezed by deformation of the main structure. A roof beam moves vertically under live load, snow or temperature; a fin fixed rigidly at its head would be loaded as a column, so the usual approach fixes the base and lets the head transfer horizontal force while sliding vertically, or hangs the fin from the head with a sliding base so the glass is in tension. The normal sequence is to set the shoes, stand and plumb the fins, install face glass and finally apply silicone, measuring the accumulated tolerance at every step.

Glass calculations are very sensitive to boundary conditions, interlayer coupling and joint stiffness, so large fins are often load-tested at full scale: on a test rig, staged static loads or a pressure chamber apply design wind and overload while deflection, lateral displacement and residual set are measured, and destructive tests reveal where cracks start and how the fin behaves after breakage. A measured deflection clearly above the calculation points to loose supports, insufficient coupling or joint slip, which must be explained before production.

Glass breakage almost always starts at an edge or hole, so site inspection concentrates on edges: grinding grade, chips, scratches and metal contact. Partial shading, heating outlets or dark films widen the temperature difference between the centre and edge of a pane and create edge tension; untoughened glass or damaged edges are most prone to thermal breakage. Toughened glass is also checked for uniform stress distribution by polarised viewing and for optical defects such as roller wave, which do not affect safety but often cause acceptance disputes with the owner.

If toughened glass contains a nickel-sulphide inclusion, the inclusion slowly changes phase and expands at ambient temperature, and years later the glass may shatter with no external load, which is spontaneous breakage. Heat soaking, for example to EN 14179, reheats toughened glass and holds it at temperature so that affected panes break in the factory, reducing but not eliminating the site risk. In a toughened-glass fin one broken ply must be carried by the remaining plies and interlayer; in the long term, moisture delamination at interlayer edges, silicone ageing and corrosion of fittings also weaken the joints.

Large fins can have a design life of decades, but at least one replacement must be expected: spontaneous breakage, impact or alteration may require a single fin or face pane to come out. Because the fin is structural, the face glass must be temporarily supported and its wind load carried before removal, so pick points, access routes and replacement-size limits must be planned in the design. When the glass cube at Apple Fifth Avenue in New York was rebuilt in 2011, fewer and larger glass units with fewer fixings replaced the original, showing how reducing the number of joints also cuts maintenance and replacement work.
evidence: 設計初期就要繪出荷重路徑圖，分別標示風壓、自重、地震與溫度變形由哪些構件與接合承擔，並列出需要主結構配合的反力與位移限制，作為帷幕牆與結構兩方介面協調的依據。
長玻璃肋應在設計說明中寫明挫屈驗算假設（初始彎曲、耦合程度、側向拘束來源），並要求在受壓自由邊設置可檢查的側向支撐或加深斷面；任何取消拘束的變更都須重新驗算。
規範要寫明中間膜種類、厚度、溫度與載重時間對應的設計剪力模數，以及一片破裂時的殘餘承載要求；玻璃廠須提交膠合製程紀錄與抽樣檢驗，替換中間膜品牌須經結構設計者重新驗算。
矽利康施作須在可控的工廠或現場淨化條件下進行，每批記錄清潔、底漆、混合比與蝴蝶試驗或斷膠試驗結果；所有金屬件與螺栓接合都要有可讀的扭力或預壓紀錄，並避免金屬直接接觸玻璃。
吊裝屬高風險作業，每一次大型玻璃吊裝都要有經核准的吊裝計畫、試吊與停止點，由起重負責人與帷幕牆工程師在現場確認後才能進行；玻璃以立式運輸架運送並全程保護邊緣。
evidenceEn: Draw a load-path diagram early, marking which members and joints carry wind, self-weight, seismic and thermal movement, and list the reactions and movement limits the main structure must accommodate, as the basis for coordinating the façade–structure interface.

For long fins the design statement must record the buckling assumptions, namely initial bow, degree of coupling and source of lateral restraint, and require an inspectable lateral restraint or a deeper section on the compressed free edge; any change that removes restraint requires a new check.

The specification must state interlayer type, thickness and design shear moduli for each temperature and load duration, plus the residual-capacity requirement with one ply broken; the glass processor must submit laminating records and sample tests, and any change of interlayer brand needs re-checking by the structural designer.

Silicone work must be done under controlled shop or clean site conditions, with each batch recording cleaning, priming, mix ratio and butterfly or snap test results; every fitting and bolted joint needs a readable torque or preload record, and metal must never touch glass directly.

Lifting is high-risk work: every major glass lift needs an approved lifting plan, a trial lift and hold points, and proceeds only after the lifting supervisor and façade engineer confirm on site; glass travels in upright transport frames with its edges protected throughout.
pitfalls: 若忽略角隅或開口處的分擔寬度變化，邊肋可能承受比中間肋高出許多的風壓；支承反力未傳達給主結構設計者時，屋頂梁可能因玻璃肋反力而過度變形，反過來把壓力推回玻璃。
以室溫短時的中間膜勁度設計，夏季正午受日照的玻璃肋實際接近不耦合狀態，挫屈承載只剩設計值的一小部分；膠合品質不良的氣泡或邊緣脫層也會讓局部變成各片獨立作用。
把長玻璃肋平放在中央單點或兩端支點上搬運，弱軸彎曲加上車輛振動足以讓玻璃開裂；翻轉時邊緣碰到地面或鋼構造成貝殼狀崩邊，安裝時看不出，數月後在風壓或溫差下自邊緣破裂。
試驗只量中央撓度而沒有量受壓邊的側向位移，挫屈前兆被忽略；或試驗樣品的支承比現場更剛硬，試驗合格但現場勁度不足，實際立面在強風時明顯晃動並有破裂風險。
結構玻璃肋全部採用未熱浸的強化玻璃且未考慮一片破裂的殘餘承載，一次自爆就可能讓整支肋失去承載，面玻璃隨之鬆脫；中間膜邊緣長期浸水造成脫層，耦合降低而增加挫屈風險。
pitfallsEn: Ignoring changes in tributary width at corners or openings can leave edge fins carrying much more wind than the middle fins; if support reactions never reach the main-structure designer, the roof beam may deflect excessively under fin reactions and push load back into the glass.

Designing with room-temperature short-term interlayer stiffness means that a fin in summer midday sun is actually close to uncoupled, leaving only a fraction of the design buckling capacity; bubbles or edge delamination from poor laminating make plies act separately in those zones.

Carrying a long fin flat on a single central support or on supports at its ends lets weak-axis bending plus vehicle vibration crack it; during tilting an edge that strikes the ground or steelwork suffers a shell chip invisible at installation that later starts a crack under wind or thermal stress months afterwards.

Measuring only mid-span deflection and not the lateral movement of the compressed edge misses the warning signs of buckling; a test rig with stiffer supports than the site lets the sample pass while the real façade lacks stiffness, swaying visibly in strong wind with a risk of breakage.

Using non-heat-soaked toughened glass throughout the fins without checking residual capacity after one ply breaks means a single spontaneous breakage can disable a whole fin and release the face glass; long-term water at interlayer edges causes delamination, reducing coupling and increasing buckling risk.

procedureEn: Compare the key figures with this course's worked example and mark which are public project data and which are teaching assumptions.

Pick one landmark project to compare with this course and list differences in span or height, structural system, main loads and construction method.
